mishnayos.summary: This mishnah teaches how many judges are needed for different kinds of court cases about money and fines. Rabbi Meir and the Sages argue about one case that might end in a death penalty.

chunks.en: Cases about money are judged by three judges.

words.note: Court cases.
Three judges.

chunks.en: Cases of stealing and of hurting someone are judged by three.
Cases of full damage and half damage,

words.note: Paying for harm that a person or his animal did.
An ox that was not known to gore pays only half.

chunks.en: paying double, and paying four or five times, are judged by three.

words.note: A thief who is caught pays back double.
A thief who sold or slaughtered a stolen ox or sheep.

chunks.en: Cases of fines for wronging a girl, and of a man who says a false bad thing about his wife, are judged by three,

words.note: He did a terrible wrong to a girl and must pay a fine.
He also did a wrong to a girl and must pay a fine.
A husband who falsely says his new wife did a sin.

chunks.en: That is what Rabbi Meir says.

words.note: A great Rabbi of the Mishnah.

chunks.en: But the Sages say,
the case of the one who says a false bad thing about his wife is judged by twenty-three,
because it may turn into a case of life and death.
chunks.explain: If his wife were found guilty, she could get a death penalty.

mishnayos.summary: How many judges are needed to give lashes, and to add an extra day to a month or an extra month to a year? Rabbi Meir says three, and Rabban Shimon ben Gamliel explains how the judges for a leap year are added.

chunks.en: Lashes are given by three judges.
chunks.st: lashes are adjudicated by three judges.

chunks.st: The intercalation of the month is performed by a panel of three judges.

words.note: Adding a thirtieth day to the month.

chunks.en: Making a year longer is done by three,
chunks.st: The intercalation of the year, meaning the decision to add an extra month to the year when necessary, is also decided by a panel of three judges;

words.note: Adding an extra month, to make a leap year.

chunks.en: That is what Rabbi Meir says.
chunks.st: this is the statement of Rabbi Meir.

chunks.en: Rabban Shimon ben Gamliel says,
chunks.st: Rabban Shimon ben Gamliel says:

chunks.en: And if they finished with three, it is a leap year.
chunks.st: And Rabban Shimon ben Gamliel concedes that if they concluded the matter with only three judges, the intercalation is valid and it is a leap year.

mishnayos.summary: The great Sanhedrin had seventy-one judges and a small Sanhedrin had twenty-three. The mishnah shows from pesukim where each number comes from, and how big a city must be to have a Sanhedrin.

chunks.he: סַנְהֶדְרִי גְדוֹלָה הָיְתָה שֶׁל שִׁבְעִים וְאֶחָד,
chunks.en: The great Sanhedrin had seventy-one judges,
chunks.st: The Great Sanhedrin was composed of seventy-one judges,

chunks.en: and the small one had twenty-three.
chunks.st: and a lesser Sanhedrin was composed of twenty-three.

chunks.he: וּמִנַּיִן לַגְּדוֹלָה שֶׁהִיא שֶׁל שִׁבְעִים וְאֶחָד,
chunks.en: And how do we know that the great one has seventy-one?
chunks.st: From where is it derived that the Great Sanhedrin was composed of seventy-one judges?

chunks.en: As it says, "Gather for Me
chunks.st: As it is stated: “Gather Me

chunks.en: seventy men from the elders of Yisrael,"
chunks.st: seventy men of the Elders of Israel,
chunks.stMore: whom you know to be the Elders of the people and officers over them, and bring them into the Tent of Meeting, and they shall stand there with you” (Numbers 11:16),

chunks.en: and Moshe is over them.
chunks.st: and together with Moses at the head of this body,

chunks.en: That makes seventy-one.
chunks.st: there are a total of seventy-one.

chunks.en: Rabbi Yehudah says, seventy.
chunks.st: Rabbi Yehuda says: Moses was indeed at the head of the body, but he is not counted as part of the group. Consequently, a future Great Sanhedrin modeled after these Elders is to be composed of seventy judges.

chunks.he: וּמִנַּיִן לַקְּטַנָּה שֶׁהִיא שֶׁל עֶשְׂרִים וּשְׁלֹשָׁה,
chunks.en: And how do we know that the small one has twenty-three?
chunks.st: And from where is it derived that a lesser Sanhedrin is composed of twenty-three judges?

chunks.en: As it says,
chunks.st: As it is stated:

chunks.en: "And the congregation shall judge..."
chunks.st: “And the congregation shall judge between the assailant and the avenger…

chunks.en: "and the congregation shall save."
chunks.st: and the congregation shall save
chunks.stMore: the manslayer from the hands of the avenger” (Numbers 35:24–25).

chunks.en: A group that judges, and a group that saves.
chunks.explain: One group tries to find him guilty, and one tries to save him.
chunks.st: Therefore, there must be a congregation, which consists of at least ten judges, that judges the accused and attempts to convict him, and there must be a congregation, also consisting of at least ten judges, which attempts to save the accused by finding him innocent.

chunks.en: That makes twenty.
chunks.st: Together, there are twenty judges here.
chunks.stMore: Before proceeding to derive the requirement for the final three judges, the mishna clarifies:

chunks.en: And how do we know that a "congregation" is ten?
chunks.st: And from where is it derived that a congregation consists of at least ten men?

chunks.en: As it says
chunks.st: As it is stated concerning the spies:

chunks.en: "How long for this bad congregation,"
chunks.explain: Hashem said this about the spies.
chunks.st: “How long shall I bear with this evil congregation
chunks.stMore: that keep complaining about me?” (Numbers 14:27) There were twelve spies;

chunks.en: without Yehoshua and Kalev.
chunks.explain: There were twelve spies; without these two, there were ten.
chunks.st: excluding Joshua and Caleb,
chunks.stMore: who did not complain, there would be ten men who are called: A congregation. Accordingly, the verses describing a congregation that attempts to convict the accused and a congregation that attempts to acquit him together add up to twenty judges.

chunks.en: And how do we know to add three more?
chunks.st: And from where is it derived to bring three more judges to the court?

chunks.en: From what it says,
chunks.st: From the implication of that which is stated:

chunks.en: "Do not follow the many to do bad,"
chunks.st: “You shall not follow a multitude to convict” (Exodus 23:2),

chunks.en: I hear that I may go with them to do good.
chunks.explain: To find him not guilty.
chunks.st: I would derive that I may not convict a person on the basis of a majority but I should follow the majority to exonerate.

chunks.en: If so, why does it say,
chunks.st: If so, why is it stated in the same verse:

chunks.en: "Lean after the many"?
chunks.st: “To incline after a multitude,”
chunks.stMore: from which it can be understood that the majority is followed in all cases? In order to resolve the apparent contradiction it must be explained:

chunks.en: Leaning to good is not like leaning to bad.
chunks.st: Your inclination after the majority to exonerate is not like your inclination after the majority to convict.

chunks.en: To lean to good, one more judge is enough.
chunks.st: Your inclination after the majority to exonerate can result in a verdict by a majority of one judge.

chunks.en: To lean to bad, you need two more.
chunks.explain: So we need twenty-two judges.
chunks.st: But your inclination after the majority to convict a transgressor must be by a more decisive majority of at least two.
chunks.stMore: Therefore, the court must have at least twenty-two judges.

chunks.en: And a court may not be an even number,
chunks.st: And since there is a principle that a court may not be composed of an even
chunks.stMore: number of judges, as such a court may be unable to reach a decision, therefore

chunks.en: so we add one more judge.
chunks.st: they add another one to them, and

chunks.en: That makes twenty-three.

chunks.en: How many people must be in a city for it to have a Sanhedrin?
chunks.st: And how many men must be in the city for it to be eligible for a lesser Sanhedrin?

chunks.st: Two hundred and thirty,

If there are not enough men in the city to enable this calculation, it would not be honorable to appoint a Sanhedrin, as their members will each preside over less than the minimum of ten residents.

mishnayos.summary: This mishnah teaches the special halachos of the Kohen Gadol: he can judge and be judged, and how he acts when a relative passes away and when people come to comfort him.

chunks.en: The Kohen Gadol judges others, and others judge him.
He gives testimony, and others give testimony about him.
He can do chalitzah, and his brother can do chalitzah to his wife,
and his brother can marry his wife in yibum,
but he himself does not do yibum,

words.note: Marrying the widow of a brother who had no children.

chunks.en: because he may not marry a widow.
If someone in his family passes away,
he does not walk after the bier.

mishnayos.summary: The king is treated differently: he does not judge, testify, or do chalitzah or yibum, because of the honor of the kingdom. Rabbi Yehudah and the Sages argue about some of these halachos.

chunks.he: הַמֶּלֶךְ לֹא דָן וְלֹא דָנִין אוֹתוֹ,
chunks.en: The king does not judge, and others do not judge him.
He does not give testimony, and others do not testify about him.
He does not do chalitzah, and his brother does not do chalitzah to his wife.
He does not do yibum, and his brother does not do yibum with his wife.

if he wants to do chalitzah or yibum,
he is remembered for good.

a king may marry the widow of a king,
because that is what we find with Dovid,
who married the widow of Shaul,
as it says,

chunks.en: Even if they are like Avigayil.
chunks.st: This teaches that even if his wives are like Abigail,
chunks.stMore: who was righteous and prevented David from sin (see I Samuel, chapter 25), it is prohibited for him to have many wives. The king

words.note: A very righteous woman who married Dovid.

chunks.en: "He shall not have too many horses,"
chunks.st: “shall not accumulate many horses for himself” (Deuteronomy 17:16),

chunks.en: only enough for his chariot.
chunks.st: but only enough for his chariot in war and in peace.

chunks.he: וְכֶסֶף וְזָהָב לֹא יַרְבֶּה לּוֹ מְאֹד (שם),

chunks.st: “Neither shall he greatly accumulate silver and gold for himself” (Deuteronomy 17:17),

chunks.en: only enough to pay his soldiers.
chunks.st: but only enough to provide his soldiers’ sustenance [aspanya].

chunks.en: And he writes a Sefer Torah for himself.
chunks.st: And the king writes himself a Torah scroll for his sake, as stipulated in Deuteronomy 17:18.

chunks.en: When he goes out to war, he takes it out with him.
chunks.st: When he goes out to war, he brings it out with him.

chunks.en: When he comes in, he brings it in with him.
chunks.st: When he comes in from war, he brings it in with him.

chunks.en: When he sits to judge, it is with him.
chunks.st: When he sits in judgment, it is with him.

chunks.en: When he sits to eat, it is in front of him,
chunks.st: When he reclines to eat, it is opposite him,

chunks.en: as it says,
chunks.st: as it is stated:

chunks.he: וְהָיְתָה עִמּוֹ וְקָרָא בוֹ כָּל יְמֵי חַיָּיו:
chunks.en: "And it shall be with him, and he shall read from it all the days of his life."
chunks.st: “And it shall be with him and he shall read it all the days of his life” (Deuteronomy 17:19).

mishnayos.summary: People must show great respect to a king, so no one may use his things, like his horse, his throne, or his scepter, or see him when he is not looking his royal best.

chunks.en: No one may ride on his horse,
chunks.st: One may not ride on the king’s horse,

chunks.en: and no one may sit on his throne,
chunks.st: and one may not sit on his throne,

chunks.en: and no one may use his scepter.
chunks.st: and one may not use his scepter,

words.note: The king's special stick.

chunks.en: And no one may see him when he is getting a haircut,
chunks.st: and one may not see him when he is having his hair cut,

chunks.he: וְלֹא כְשֶׁהוּא עָרֹם וְלֹא בְבֵית הַמֶּרְחָץ,
chunks.en: nor when he is not dressed, nor in the bathhouse,
chunks.st: nor when he is naked, nor when he is in the bathhouse,

chunks.en: as it says, "You shall surely set a king over you,"
chunks.st: as it is stated: “You shall set a king over you” (Deuteronomy 17:15),

chunks.en: so that the fear of him is on you.
chunks.st: meaning, ensure that his fear should be upon you.
chunks.stMore: All of these actions would lessen one’s fear of and reverence for the king.

mishnayos.summary: For money cases, each side chooses a judge and a third judge is added. The mishnah also teaches when one side can turn down the other side's judge or witnesses.

chunks.en: Money cases are judged by three.
chunks.st: Cases of monetary law are adjudicated by three. They are chosen in the following manner:

chunks.en: This one chooses one judge for himself,
chunks.st: This litigant chooses one for himself

chunks.en: and that one chooses one judge for himself,
chunks.st: and that litigant chooses one for himself,

chunks.en: and the two of them choose one more.
chunks.st: and the two of them choose one more for themselves;

chunks.en: That is what Rabbi Meir says.
chunks.st: this is the statement of Rabbi Meir.

chunks.en: But the Sages say,
chunks.st: And the Rabbis say:

chunks.he: שְׁנֵי דַיָּנִין בּוֹרְרִין לָהֶן עוֹד אֶחָד.
chunks.en: the two judges choose one more.
chunks.st: The two judges that were chosen choose one more judge for themselves.

chunks.en: This one can turn down that one's judge,
chunks.st: This litigant can disqualify the judge chosen by that litigant

chunks.en: and that one can turn down this one's judge.
chunks.st: and that litigant can disqualify the judge chosen by this litigant;

chunks.en: That is what Rabbi Meir says.
chunks.st: this is the statement of Rabbi Meir.

chunks.en: But the Sages say,
chunks.st: And the Rabbis say:

chunks.en: when is that? When he brings proof about them
chunks.st: When can one of the litigants disqualify the judges? Only when he brings evidence about them

chunks.en: that they are relatives or not fit to judge.
chunks.st: that they are related to one of the litigants or to each other, or that they are disqualified from serving as judges for another reason.

chunks.he: אֲבָל אִם הָיוּ כְשֵׁרִים אוֹ מֻמְחִין,
chunks.en: But if they are fit judges, or experts,
chunks.st: But if they are fit to serve as judges or are experts ordained by the court,

words.note: Judges who got semichah.

chunks.en: he cannot turn them down.
chunks.st: he cannot disqualify them.

chunks.en: This one can turn down that one's witnesses,
chunks.st: This litigant can disqualify the witnesses of that litigant

chunks.en: and that one can turn down this one's witnesses.
chunks.st: and that litigant can disqualify the witnesses of this litigant;

chunks.en: That is what Rabbi Meir says.
chunks.st: this is the statement of Rabbi Meir.

chunks.en: But the Sages say,
chunks.st: And the Rabbis say:

chunks.he: אֵימָתַי, בִּזְמַן שֶׁהוּא מֵבִיא עֲלֵיהֶם רְאָיָה
chunks.en: when is that? When he brings proof about them
chunks.st: When can one litigant disqualify the other’s witnesses? Only when he brings evidence about them

chunks.en: that they are relatives or not fit to be witnesses.
chunks.st: that they are related to one of the litigants or to each other, or that they are disqualified from bearing witness for another reason.

chunks.en: But if they are fit,
chunks.st: But if they are fit to serve as witnesses,

chunks.en: he cannot turn them down.
chunks.st: he cannot disqualify them.

mishnayos.summary: What if a person agrees to let someone who is not a proper judge decide his case, or agrees to let the other side make a promise instead of a real shevuah? Can he change his mind?

chunks.en: If one said to the other, "I trust my father to judge my case,"
chunks.st: If one litigant says to the other: My father is trusted to adjudicate for me, or:

chunks.en: or "I trust your father,"
chunks.st: Your father is trusted to adjudicate for me, or:

chunks.en: or "I trust three cowherds,"
chunks.explain: People who do not know the halachos well.
chunks.st: Three cattle herders, who are not proficient in halakha, are trusted to adjudicate for me,
chunks.stMore: all of whom are disqualified from serving as judges,

chunks.en: Rabbi Meir says,
chunks.st: Rabbi Meir says:

chunks.en: he can change his mind.
chunks.st: The one who made the offer can retract it,

chunks.en: But the Sages say,
chunks.st: and the Rabbis say:

chunks.en: he cannot change his mind.
chunks.st: He cannot retract it, but must accept their verdict.

chunks.en: If he had to swear a shevuah to his friend,
chunks.st: Similarly, one who was obligated by Torah law to take an oath to another, which is done while grasping a sacred object,

words.note: A very serious promise made holding a holy object.

chunks.he: וְאָמַר לוֹ דּוֹר לִי בְחַיֵּי רֹאשְׁךָ,
chunks.en: and his friend said to him, "Just make a promise to me on the life of your head,"
chunks.st: and the latter said to him: Instead of taking an oath, merely vow to me by the life of your head that what you claim is true,

chunks.en: Rabbi Meir says,
chunks.st: Rabbi Meir says:

chunks.en: he can change his mind.
chunks.st: The one who made the offer can retract it,
chunks.stMore: and demand that the other litigant take an oath, as he is obligated to do by Torah law.

chunks.en: But the Sages say,
chunks.st: And the Rabbis say:

chunks.en: he cannot change his mind.
chunks.st: He cannot retract
chunks.stMore: his offer. Once he has agreed to accept a vow, which is of less severity than an oath, he cannot retract his agreement.

mishnayos.summary: Some people may not be witnesses because they make money in dishonest ways, like gamblers and people who lend with interest. Rabbi Yehudah says this is only when it is their only job.

chunks.en: These are the people who are not fit to be witnesses:
chunks.st: And these on the following list are the ones who are disqualified
chunks.stMore: by the Sages from bearing witness due to their unseemly behavior, as they are considered wicked individuals guilty of monetary transgressions:

chunks.en: one who plays with dice for money,
chunks.st: One who plays with dice [bekubbiyya] for money,

chunks.en: and one who lends with interest,
chunks.st: and one who lends money with interest,

words.note: Ribbis: extra money the Torah forbids taking for a loan.

chunks.en: and those who race pigeons,
chunks.st: and those who fly pigeons,

words.note: They bet money on which bird wins.

chunks.en: and those who sell Shemittah fruit.
chunks.st: and merchants who trade in the produce of the Sabbatical
chunks.stMore: Year, which may be eaten but may not be sold as an object of commerce.

words.note: Fruit of the seventh year may not be bought and sold for business.

chunks.en: Rabbi Shimon said,
chunks.st: Rabbi Shimon said:

chunks.he: בִּתְחִלָּה הָיוּ קוֹרִין אוֹתָן אוֹסְפֵי שְׁבִיעִית,
chunks.en: At first they called them "gatherers of Shemittah fruit."
chunks.st: Initially, people would call them: Gatherers of the produce of the Sabbatical Year.

chunks.en: Once the tax collectors became many,
chunks.st: Once the tax collectors grew abundant

chunks.en: they went back to calling them "traders of Shemittah fruit."
chunks.st: they would then call them: Merchants who trade in the produce of the Sabbatical Year, as the Gemara will explain.

chunks.en: Rabbi Yehudah said,
chunks.st: Rabbi Yehuda said:

chunks.he: אֵימָתַי, בִּזְמַן שֶׁאֵין לָהֶם אֻמָּנוּת אֶלָּא הִיא,
chunks.en: When is this? When they have no other job but this.
chunks.st: When are the people listed above disqualified from bearing witness? It is when they have no occupation but this one.

chunks.he: אֲבָל יֵשׁ לָהֶן אֻמָּנוּת שֶׁלֹּא הִיא, כְּשֵׁרִין:
chunks.en: But if they have another job, they are fit.
chunks.st: But if they have an occupation other than this one, although they also make money by these inappropriate means, they are fit to bear witness.

mishnayos.summary: Relatives may not be witnesses or judges for each other. The mishnah lists which relatives, and teaches what happens if someone stops being a relative.

chunks.en: These are the relatives:
chunks.st: And these are the ones disqualified from bearing witness or from serving as judges due to their status as relatives of one of the litigants or of each other:

chunks.he: אָבִיו וְאָחִיו וַאֲחִי אָבִיו וַאֲחִי אִמּוֹ
chunks.en: his father, his brother, his father's brother, his mother's brother,
chunks.st: One’s father, brother, and his paternal uncle, and his maternal uncle,

chunks.en: his sister's husband, his father's sister's husband,
chunks.st: and his sister’s husband, and the husband of his paternal aunt,

chunks.en: his mother's sister's husband,
chunks.st: and the husband of his maternal aunt,

chunks.en: his mother's husband, his father-in-law, and his brother-in-law,
chunks.st: and his mother’s husband, and his father-in-law, and his brother-in-law, i.e., the husband of his wife’s sister.

chunks.en: they, and their sons, and their sons-in-law,
chunks.st: They themselves, all of these people, and also their sons, and their sons-in-law are considered relatives.

chunks.en: and his stepson only.
chunks.st: And his stepson alone
chunks.stMore: is disqualified, but not his stepson’s sons or sons-in-law.

chunks.en: Rabbi Yosei said,
chunks.st: Rabbi Yosei says:

chunks.en: this is the mishnah of Rabbi Akiva.
chunks.st: This aforementioned halakha is Rabbi Akiva’s version of the mishna.

chunks.en: But the first mishnah said:
chunks.st: But the initial version of the mishna reads as follows:

chunks.en: His uncle and his uncle's son,
chunks.st: His uncle and the son of his uncle,

chunks.en: and anyone who could inherit from him,
chunks.st: and anyone who is fit to inherit from him.
chunks.stMore: Only paternal relatives, who are fit to inherit from him, are disqualified; maternal relatives, who do not inherit from him, are not disqualified from bearing witness about him or from adjudicating his case.

chunks.en: and anyone who is related to him at that time.
chunks.st: And the halakha disqualifying a relative from bearing witness or serving as a judge is referring to anyone who is related to him at the time of the trial.

chunks.en: If he was a relative and then stopped being related,
chunks.st: If one was once a relative and became unrelated
chunks.stMore: by the time of the trial, e.g., he married the daughter of one of the litigants, but she died or they were divorced,

chunks.en: he is fit.
chunks.st: in this case he is fit.

chunks.en: Rabbi Yehudah says,
chunks.st: Rabbi Yehuda says:

chunks.en: even if his daughter passed away,
chunks.st: Even if his daughter died

chunks.en: but he has children from her,
chunks.st: but her husband, the former son-in-law, has children from her,

chunks.en: he is still a relative.
chunks.st: he is still considered a relative; the children cause them to remain related.

mishnayos.summary: A close friend or an enemy of one side may not be a witness or a judge. The Sages say Jews are not suspected of lying for that reason.

chunks.en: The one who loves and the one who hates.
chunks.st: One who loves or one who hates one of the litigants is also disqualified.

chunks.en: "The one who loves" is his best man at his wedding.
chunks.st: With regard to one who loves one of the litigants, this is referring to his groomsman.

chunks.en: "The one who hates" is anyone who did not speak with him
chunks.st: One who hates is referring to anyone who, out of enmity, did not speak with the litigant for

chunks.en: for three days because he was angry at him.
chunks.st: three days.

chunks.en: They said to him,
chunks.st: The Rabbis said to Rabbi Yehuda:

chunks.en: Jews are not suspected of that.
chunks.st: The Jewish people are not suspected of bearing false witness due to love or hate.

mishnayos.summary: The judges check the witnesses one at a time to make sure they tell the truth. Then the judges discuss the case and decide by a majority.

chunks.en: How do they check the witnesses?
chunks.st: How do the judges examine the witnesses?

chunks.en: They bring them in and warn them to tell the truth.
chunks.st: They bring them into a room in the courthouse and intimidate them so that they will speak only the truth.

chunks.en: They send everyone else outside,
chunks.st: And they take all the people, other than the judges, outside
chunks.stMore: so that they should not tell the other witnesses the questions the judges ask and the answers the first witness gives,

chunks.en: and they leave only the oldest of them.
chunks.st: and they leave only the eldest of the witnesses to testify first.

chunks.en: And they say to him, "Tell us,
chunks.st: And they say to him: Say

chunks.he: הֵיאַךְ אַתָּה יוֹדֵעַ שֶׁזֶּה חַיָּב לָזֶה.
chunks.en: how do you know that this one owes money to that one?"
chunks.st: how exactly you know that this litigant owes money to that litigant, as the plaintiff claims.

chunks.en: If he said,
chunks.st: If he said:

chunks.he: הוּא אָמַר לִי שֶׁאֲנִי חַיָּב לוֹ,
chunks.en: "He told me that he owes him,"
chunks.st: The defendant said to me: It is true that I owe the plaintiff, or if he says:

chunks.he: אִישׁ פְּלוֹנִי אָמַר לִי שֶׁהוּא חַיָּב לוֹ,
chunks.en: or "A certain man told me that he owes him,"
chunks.st: So-and-so said to me that the defendant owes the plaintiff,

chunks.en: he has said nothing.
chunks.st: the witness has said nothing and his testimony is disregarded.

chunks.en: It does not count until he says,
chunks.st: It is not valid testimony unless he says:

chunks.en: "In front of us he admitted
chunks.st: The defendant admitted in our presence to the plaintiff

chunks.en: that he owes him two hundred zuz."
chunks.st: that he owes him, e.g., two hundred dinars.
chunks.stMore: By admitting to the debt in the presence of witnesses he renders himself liable to pay the amount that he mentioned.

words.note: A kind of coin.

chunks.en: Afterward they bring in the second witness
chunks.st: And afterward they bring in the second witness

chunks.en: and check him.
chunks.st: and examine him in the same manner.

chunks.en: If what they say matches,
chunks.st: If their statements are found to be congruent

chunks.en: the judges discuss the case.
chunks.explain: They talk it over and give reasons.
chunks.st: the judges then discuss the matter.

chunks.en: If two judges say "not guilty,"
chunks.st: If the opinions of the judges are divided, as two judges say that the defendant is exempt from payment

chunks.en: and one says "guilty," he is not guilty.
chunks.st: and one says he is liable to pay, he is exempt.

chunks.en: If two say "guilty,"
chunks.st: If two say he is liable

chunks.en: and one says "not guilty," he is guilty.
chunks.st: and one says he is exempt, he is liable.

chunks.en: If one says "not guilty,"
chunks.st: If one says he is liable

chunks.en: and one says "guilty,"
chunks.st: and one says he is exempt,

chunks.en: or even if two say "not guilty"
chunks.st: or even if two of the judges deem him exempt

chunks.en: or two say "guilty,"
chunks.st: or two of them deem him liable,

chunks.en: and one says "I do not know,"
chunks.st: and the other one says: I do not know,

chunks.en: they must add more judges.
chunks.st: the court must add more judges
chunks.stMore: and then rule in accordance with the majority opinion. This is because the one who abstains is considered as though he is not a member of the court.

mishnayos.summary: When the judges finish, the head judge tells each side the decision. A judge may not tell anyone afterward that he disagreed with the others, because that is like tale-bearing.

chunks.en: When they finished deciding the case,
chunks.st: After the judges finish the matter and reach a decision,

chunks.en: they would bring the two sides in.
chunks.st: they bring in the litigants.

chunks.en: The biggest of the judges says,
chunks.st: The greatest of the judges says:

chunks.en: "So-and-so, you are not guilty,"
chunks.st: So-and-so, you are exempt from paying; or:

chunks.en: or "So-and-so, you are guilty."
chunks.st: So-and-so, you are liable to pay.

chunks.en: And how do we know that when one of the judges goes out
chunks.st: And from where is it derived that when the judge leaves the courtroom

chunks.en: he may not say, "I said not guilty,
chunks.st: he may not say: I deemed you exempt

chunks.en: and my friends said guilty,
chunks.st: and my colleagues deemed you liable,

chunks.he: אֲבָל מָה אֶעֱשֶׂה שֶׁחֲבֵרַי רַבּוּ עָלָי,
chunks.en: but what can I do, my friends were more than me"?
chunks.st: but what can I do, as my colleagues outnumbered me and consequently you were deemed liable?

chunks.en: About this it says,
chunks.st: About this it is stated:

chunks.en: "Do not go around as a tale-bearer among your people,"
chunks.st: “You shall not go as a talebearer among your people” (Leviticus 19:16),

chunks.he: וְאוֹמֵר הוֹלֵךְ רָכִיל מְגַלֶּה סּוֹד (משלי יא):
chunks.en: and it says, "One who goes around as a tale-bearer tells secrets."
chunks.st: and it says: “One who goes about as a talebearer reveals secrets,
chunks.stMore: but one who is of a faithful spirit conceals a matter” (Proverbs 11:13).

mishnayos.summary: If someone finds new proof after his case was decided, can he change the ruling? The Sages and Rabban Shimon ben Gamliel argue about proof found late, but all agree that hidden proof brought at the last moment is worthless.

chunks.en: As long as he brings proof,
chunks.st: Any time one of the litigants brings additional proof,

chunks.en: he can undo the ruling.
chunks.st: he can overturn the verdict
chunks.stMore: that was decided according to previous proofs.

chunks.en: If they said to him,
chunks.st: If one litigant said to the other:

chunks.en: "Bring all the proof you have
chunks.st: Bring all the proofs that you have

chunks.en: from now until thirty days,"
chunks.st: from now until thirty days from now,

chunks.en: if he found it within thirty days, he can undo the ruling.
chunks.st: if he found additional proof within thirty days, he can overturn the verdict.

chunks.en: After thirty days, he cannot undo it.
chunks.st: If he found it after thirty days, he cannot overturn the verdict anymore.

chunks.en: Rabban Shimon ben Gamliel said,
chunks.st: Rabban Shimon ben Gamliel said:

chunks.en: "What can this person do,
chunks.st: He can still overturn the verdict, as what should this litigant,

chunks.en: who did not find it within thirty days,
chunks.st: who sought and did not find additional proof within thirty days

chunks.en: and found it after thirty?"
chunks.explain: So he can still undo the ruling.
chunks.st: but found it after thirty days, have done?

chunks.en: If they said to him, "Bring witnesses,"
chunks.st: In a case where one litigant said to the other: Bring witnesses,

chunks.en: and he said, "I have no witnesses,"
chunks.st: and the latter said: I have no witnesses,

chunks.en: and they said, "Bring proof,"
chunks.st: and the former said to him: Bring a proof,

chunks.en: and he said, "I have no proof,"
chunks.st: and he said: I have no proof,

chunks.he: וּלְאַחַר זְמָן הֵבִיא רְאָיָה וּמָצָא עֵדִים,
chunks.en: and later he brought proof or found witnesses,
chunks.st: and he later brought a proof or found witnesses,

chunks.en: it is worth nothing.
chunks.st: in this case, this proof or these witnesses are worth nothing.
chunks.stMore: It is apparently a false proof or false testimony.

chunks.en: Rabban Shimon ben Gamliel said,
chunks.st: Rabban Shimon ben Gamliel said:

chunks.en: "What can this person do,
chunks.st: What should this litigant,

chunks.he: שֶׁלֹּא הָיָה יוֹדֵעַ שֶׁיֶּשׁ לוֹ עֵדִים
chunks.en: who did not know that he had witnesses,
chunks.st: who did not know that he has witnesses

chunks.en: and then found witnesses,
chunks.st: and ultimately found witnesses,

chunks.he: לֹא הָיָה יוֹדֵעַ שֶׁיֶּשׁ לוֹ רְאָיָה
chunks.en: or did not know that he had proof,
chunks.st: or who did not know that he has a proof

chunks.en: and then found proof?"
chunks.st: and ultimately found proof, have done? Therefore, he can still overturn the verdict.

chunks.en: If they said to him, "Bring witnesses,"
chunks.st: If at the beginning of the discussion in the court

chunks.he: אָמַר אֵין לִי עֵדִים, הָבֵא רְאָיָה
chunks.en: and he said, "I have no witnesses"; "Bring proof,"
chunks.st: one did not bring witnesses

chunks.en: and he said, "I have no proof,"
chunks.st: or other evidence for his claims,

chunks.en: and then he saw he was about to lose the case,
chunks.st: but then he saw that he was about to be deemed liable to pay in the judgment,

chunks.en: and he said, "Bring over so-and-so and so-and-so to be my witnesses,"
chunks.st: and said: Bring so-and-so and so-and-so, and they will testify on my behalf,

words.en: and let them testify for me

chunks.en: or he took out proof from his belt,
chunks.st: or he pulled out a proof from under his belt [pundato],

chunks.en: it is worth nothing.
chunks.explain: If it were true, he would not have hidden it until now.
chunks.st: even Rabban Shimon ben Gamliel holds that this is worth nothing.
chunks.stMore: If there was truth in the testimony of these witnesses or in this proof, he would not have hidden it until now.

mishnayos.summary: Money cases and life-and-death cases both need careful questioning of the witnesses. But in many ways the court is much more careful in life-and-death cases, always looking for a way to save the person.

chunks.he: אֶחָד דִּינֵי מָמוֹנוֹת וְאֶחָד דִּינֵי נְפָשׁוֹת,
chunks.en: Both money cases and life-and-death cases
chunks.st: Both cases of monetary law and cases of capital law are equal with regard to

chunks.en: need careful questioning of the witnesses,
chunks.st: the requirement for inquiry and interrogation of the witnesses,

chunks.en: as it says,
chunks.st: as it is stated:

chunks.en: "You shall have one law."
chunks.st: “You shall have one manner of law”
chunks.stMore: (Leviticus 24:22), meaning that all legal procedures must be uniform. Having stated the essential similarity between the two, the mishna enumerates the differences between them.

chunks.he: מַה בֵּין דִּינֵי מָמוֹנוֹת לְדִינֵי נְפָשׁוֹת.
chunks.en: What is the difference between money cases and life-and-death cases?
chunks.st: What are the differences between cases of monetary law and cases of capital law?

chunks.en: Money cases are judged by three,
chunks.st: Cases of monetary law are judged by a court of three judges,

chunks.en: and life-and-death cases by twenty-three.
chunks.st: and cases of capital law are judged by a court of twenty-three judges.

chunks.en: In money cases, the judges may start
chunks.st: In cases of monetary law, the court opens the deliberations

chunks.en: with a reason for "not guilty" or for "guilty."
chunks.st: either with a claim to exempt the accused, or with a claim to find him liable.

chunks.en: In life-and-death cases, they start with a reason for "not guilty,"
chunks.st: And in cases of capital law, the court opens the deliberations with a claim to acquit the accused,

chunks.en: and they do not start with "guilty."
chunks.st: but it does not open the deliberations with a claim to find him liable.

chunks.he: דִּינֵי מָמוֹנוֹת מַטִּין עַל פִּי אֶחָד
chunks.en: In money cases, one extra judge is enough to decide
chunks.st: In cases of monetary law, the court directs, i.e., issues, the ruling based on a majority of one judge,

chunks.en: either "not guilty" or "guilty."
chunks.st: either to exempt, or to find liable.

chunks.he: וְדִינֵי נְפָשׁוֹת מַטִּין עַל פִּי אֶחָד לִזְכוּת
chunks.en: In life-and-death cases, one extra judge is enough for "not guilty,"
chunks.st: But in cases of capital law, the court directs the judgment based on a majority of one judge to acquit

chunks.en: but for "guilty" you need two extra.
chunks.st: and based on a majority of two judges to find liable.

chunks.en: In money cases, they may open the case again
chunks.st: In cases of monetary law, the court brings the accused back to be judged again if new evidence arises,

chunks.en: for "not guilty" or for "guilty."
chunks.st: either with a claim to exempt the accused, or with a claim to find him liable.

chunks.en: In life-and-death cases, they open it again for "not guilty,"
chunks.st: In cases of capital law, the court brings the accused back to be judged again with a claim to acquit him,

chunks.en: but not for "guilty."
chunks.st: but the court does not bring him back to be judged with a claim to find him liable.

chunks.he: דִּינֵי מָמוֹנוֹת הַכֹּל מְלַמְּדִין זְכוּת וְחוֹבָה,
chunks.en: In money cases, everyone may give a reason for "not guilty" or "guilty."
chunks.st: In cases of monetary law, all those present at the trial may teach a reason to exempt a litigant or to find him liable.

chunks.en: In life-and-death cases, everyone may give a reason for "not guilty,"
chunks.st: In cases of capital law, all those present at the trial may teach a reason to acquit the accused,

chunks.en: but not everyone may give a reason for "guilty."
chunks.explain: Only the judges may.
chunks.st: but not all present may teach a reason to find him liable.
chunks.stMore: Only the judges can teach a reason to find him liable.

chunks.he: דִּינֵי מָמוֹנוֹת הַמְלַמֵּד חוֹבָה מְלַמֵּד זְכוּת
chunks.en: In money cases, a judge who gave a reason for "guilty" may give one for "not guilty,"
chunks.st: In cases of monetary law, one who initially teaches a reason to find the accused liable may then teach a reason to exempt him,

chunks.en: and one who gave a reason for "not guilty" may give one for "guilty."
chunks.st: and one who initially teaches a reason to exempt him may then teach a reason to find him liable.

chunks.he: דִּינֵי נְפָשׁוֹת הַמְלַמֵּד חוֹבָה מְלַמֵּד זְכוּת,
chunks.en: In life-and-death cases, one who said "guilty" may switch to "not guilty,"
chunks.st: In cases of capital law, one who initially teaches a reason to find him liable may then teach a reason to acquit,

chunks.en: but one who said "not guilty"
chunks.st: but one who initially teaches a reason to acquit

chunks.en: may not switch back to "guilty."
chunks.st: may not return and teach a reason to find him liable.

chunks.he: דִּינֵי מָמוֹנוֹת דָּנִין בַּיּוֹם וְגוֹמְרִין בַּלַּיְלָה,
chunks.en: Money cases are judged in the day, and may be finished at night.
chunks.st: In cases of monetary law, the court judges during the daytime, and may conclude the deliberations and issue the ruling even at night.

chunks.he: דִּינֵי נְפָשׁוֹת דָּנִין בַּיּוֹם וְגוֹמְרִין בַּיּוֹם.
chunks.en: Life-and-death cases are judged in the day, and finished in the day.
chunks.st: In cases of capital law, the court judges during the daytime, and concludes the deliberations and issues the ruling only in the daytime.

chunks.en: Money cases may be finished on the same day,
chunks.st: In cases of monetary law, the court may conclude the deliberations and issue the ruling even on that same day,

chunks.en: whether for "not guilty" or for "guilty."
chunks.st: whether to exempt the accused or to find him liable.

chunks.he: דִּינֵי נְפָשׁוֹת גּוֹמְרִין בּוֹ בַיּוֹם לִזְכוּת
chunks.en: Life-and-death cases may be finished on the same day for "not guilty,"
chunks.st: In cases of capital law, the court may conclude the deliberations and issue the ruling even on that same day to acquit the accused,

chunks.en: but only on the next day for "guilty."
chunks.st: but must wait until the following day to find him liable.

chunks.en: So we do not judge them
chunks.st: Therefore, since capital cases might continue for two days, the court does not judge cases of capital law on certain days,

chunks.en: not on Erev Shabbos,
chunks.st: neither on the eve of Shabbat

chunks.en: and not on Erev Yom Tov.
chunks.explain: The case might need a second day, which would be Shabbos or Yom Tov.
chunks.st: nor the eve of a Festival.

mishnayos.summary: This mishnah teaches which judge speaks first in different cases, and who may be a judge in life-and-death cases.

chunks.he: דִּינֵי הַטֻּמְאוֹת וְהַטָּהֳרוֹת מַתְחִילִין מִן הַגָּדוֹל,
chunks.en: In cases of tumah and taharah, the judges start with the greatest judge.
chunks.st: In cases of monetary law, and likewise in the cases of ritual impurity and purity, the judges commence expressing their opinions from the greatest of the judges.

words.note: Halachos of what is tamei and tahor.

chunks.en: In life-and-death cases, they start from the side.
chunks.explain: The smaller judges speak first, so they are not afraid to disagree with the great ones.
chunks.st: In cases of capital law, the judges commence issuing their opinions from the side, where the least significant judges sit.

chunks.en: Everyone may judge money cases,
chunks.st: All are fit to judge cases of monetary law.

chunks.he: וְאֵין הַכֹּל כְּשֵׁרִין לָדוּן דִּינֵי נְפָשׁוֹת,
chunks.en: but not everyone may judge life-and-death cases,
chunks.st: But not all are fit to judge cases of capital law;

chunks.en: only Kohanim, Levi'im,
chunks.st: only priests, Levites,

chunks.en: and Yisraelim whose daughters may marry Kohanim.
chunks.explain: Families with a clean, proper yichus.
chunks.st: and Israelites who are of sufficiently fit lineage to marry their daughters to members of the priesthood are fit to judge cases of capital law.

mishnayos.summary: The Sanhedrin sat in a half circle so all the judges could see each other. Scribes wrote down what each judge said.

chunks.en: The Sanhedrin sat like half of a round threshing floor,
chunks.st: A Sanhedrin of twenty-three was arranged in the same layout as half of a circular threshing floor,

words.note: A flat place where grain is threshed.

chunks.he: כְּדֵי שֶׁיְּהוּ רוֹאִין זֶה אֶת זֶה.
chunks.en: so that they could see one another.
chunks.st: in order that all the judges will see one another and the witnesses.

chunks.en: And two scribes of the judges stand in front of them,
chunks.st: And two judges’ scribes stand before the court,

chunks.en: one on the right and one on the left,
chunks.st: one on the right and one on the left,

chunks.en: and they write the words of those who say "not guilty" and those who say "guilty."
chunks.st: and they write the statements of those who find the accused liable and the statements of those who acquit the accused.

chunks.en: Rabbi Yehudah says, three.
chunks.st: Rabbi Yehuda says: There were three scribes.

chunks.en: One writes the words of those who say "not guilty,"
chunks.st: One writes only the statements of those who acquit the accused,

chunks.en: and one writes the words of those who say "guilty,"
chunks.st: one writes only the statements of those who find him liable,

chunks.he: וְהַשְּׁלִישִׁי כוֹתֵב דִּבְרֵי הַמְזַכִּין וְדִבְרֵי הַמְחַיְּבִין:
chunks.en: and the third writes both.
chunks.st: and the third writes both the statements of those who acquit the accused and the statements of those who find him liable,
chunks.stMore: so that if there is uncertainty concerning the precise wording that one of the scribes writes, it can be compared to the words of the third scribe.

mishnayos.summary: Three rows of talmidei chachamim sat in front of the Sanhedrin. When a new judge was needed, they took him from the first row, and everyone moved up.

chunks.en: And three rows of talmidei chachamim
chunks.st: And three rows of Torah scholars

chunks.en: sit in front of them,
chunks.st: sit before the judges, and

chunks.he: כָּל אֶחָד וְאֶחָד מַכִּיר אֶת מְקוֹמוֹ.
chunks.en: each one knows his place.
chunks.st: each and every one among those sitting recognizes his place,
chunks.stMore: i.e., they are seated in accordance with their stature.

chunks.en: If they needed to give semichah to a new judge,
chunks.st: When the court must ordain
chunks.stMore: an additional judge, e.g., if a judge dies during the proceedings or in the case of a court without a decisive majority (see 40a), the court

chunks.en: they took him from the first row.
chunks.st: ordains the greatest Torah scholar from the first row.

chunks.he: אֶחָד מִן הַשְּׁנִיָּה בָּא לוֹ לָרִאשׁוֹנָה
chunks.en: One from the second row moves to the first,
chunks.st: As a seat in the first row is now vacant, one Torah scholar from the second row comes to the first row,

chunks.he: וְאֶחָד מִן הַשְּׁלִישִׁית בָּא לוֹ לַשְּׁנִיָּה,
chunks.en: and one from the third row moves to the second,
chunks.st: and one Torah scholar from the third row comes to the second row,

chunks.he: וּבוֹרְרִין לָהֶן עוֹד אֶחָד מִן הַקָּהָל
chunks.en: and they choose one more from the crowd
chunks.st: and the court selects another Torah scholar from among the assembled

chunks.en: and seat him in the third row.
chunks.st: and they seat him in the third row.

chunks.he: וְלֹא הָיָה יוֹשֵׁב בִּמְקוֹמוֹ שֶׁל רִאשׁוֹן,
chunks.en: He would not sit in the seat of the first one,
chunks.st: And this Torah scholar who moves from the second row to the first row would not sit in the place of the first Torah scholar, who joined the court,

chunks.en: but he sits in the place that fits him.
chunks.st: rather, he would sit in the place appropriate for him,
chunks.stMore: i.e., at the end of that row, in accordance with his stature.

mishnayos.summary: Before witnesses testify in a life-and-death case, the judges warn them how serious it is. Every person is like a whole world, because Hashem created Adam alone, and each person must say, "The world was created for me."

chunks.en: How do they warn the witnesses
chunks.st: How does the court intimidate the witnesses in giving

chunks.en: in life-and-death cases?
chunks.st: testimony for cases of capital law?

chunks.en: They would bring them in and warn them:
chunks.st: They would bring the witnesses in and intimidate them by saying to them:

chunks.en: "Maybe you are saying it from a guess,
chunks.st: Perhaps what you say in your testimony is based on conjecture,

chunks.en: or from a rumor, or from one witness who heard from another,
chunks.st: or perhaps it is based on a rumor, perhaps it is testimony based on hearsay,
chunks.stMore: e.g., you heard a witness testify to this in a different court,

chunks.en: or 'We heard it from a trusted person.'
chunks.st: or perhaps it is based on the statement of a trusted person.

chunks.en: Or maybe you do not know
chunks.st: Perhaps you do not know

chunks.en: that in the end we will check you with careful questions.
chunks.st: that ultimately we examine you with inquiry and interrogation,
chunks.stMore: and if you are lying, your lie will be discovered.

chunks.en: You should know
chunks.st: The court tells them: You should know that

chunks.en: that life-and-death cases are not like money cases.
chunks.st: cases of capital law are not like cases of monetary law.

chunks.en: In money cases,
chunks.st: In cases of monetary law,

chunks.en: a person pays money and he is forgiven.
chunks.explain: If he lied, he can pay back and be forgiven.
chunks.st: a person who testifies falsely, causing money to be given to the wrong party, can give the money to the proper owner and his sin is atoned for.

chunks.en: In life-and-death cases,
chunks.st: In cases of capital law, if one testifies falsely,

chunks.en: the blood of the person and of all his children who would have been born are on him
chunks.st: the blood of the accused and the blood of his offspring that he did not merit to produce are ascribed to the witness’s testimony

chunks.en: until the end of the world.
chunks.st: until eternity.

chunks.he: שֶׁכֵּן מָצִינוּ בְקַיִן שֶׁהָרַג אֶת אָחִיו,
chunks.en: That is what we find with Kayin, who killed his brother,
chunks.st: The proof for this is as we found with Cain, who killed his brother,

chunks.en: as it says, 'The bloods of your brother cry out.'
chunks.st: as it is stated concerning him: “The voice of your brother’s blood [demei] cries out to Me from the ground” (Genesis 4:10).

chunks.en: It does not say 'the blood of your brother,'
chunks.st: The verse does not state: Your brother’s blood [dam], in the singular,

chunks.en: but 'the bloods of your brother':
chunks.st: but rather: “Your brother’s blood [demei],” in the plural.

chunks.en: his blood and the blood of his children.
chunks.st: This serves to teach that the loss of both his brother’s blood and the blood of his brother’s offspring are ascribed to Cain.

chunks.en: Another explanation:
chunks.st: The mishna notes: Alternatively,

chunks.en: 'the bloods of your brother'
chunks.st: the phrase “your brother’s blood [demei],” written in the plural,

chunks.en: means that his blood was spilled
chunks.st: teaches that that his blood was not gathered in one place but was

chunks.en: on the trees and on the stones.
chunks.st: splattered on the trees and on the stones.

chunks.en: That is why Adam was created alone,
chunks.st: The court tells the witnesses: Therefore, Adam the first man was created alone,

chunks.he: לְלַמֶּדְךָ, שֶׁכָּל הַמְאַבֵּד נֶפֶשׁ אַחַת מִיִּשְׂרָאֵל,
chunks.en: to teach you that anyone who destroys one Jewish life,
chunks.st: to teach you that with regard to anyone who destroys one soul from the Jewish people, i.e., kills one Jew,

chunks.en: the Torah counts it for him
chunks.st: the verse ascribes him blame

chunks.en: as if he destroyed a whole world.
chunks.st: as if he destroyed an entire world,
chunks.stMore: as Adam was one person, from whom the population of an entire world came forth.

chunks.en: And anyone who saves one Jewish life,
chunks.st: And conversely, anyone who sustains one soul from the Jewish people,

chunks.en: the Torah counts it for him
chunks.st: the verse ascribes him credit

chunks.en: as if he saved a whole world.
chunks.st: as if he sustained an entire world.
chunks.stMore: The mishna cites another reason Adam the first man was created alone:

chunks.en: And it was also for peace among people,
chunks.st: And this was done due to the importance of maintaining peace among people,

chunks.en: so that no person can say to his friend,
chunks.st: so that one person will not say to another:

chunks.en: 'My father is greater than your father.'
chunks.explain: Everyone comes from the same first father, Adam.
chunks.st: My father, i.e., progenitor, is greater than your father.

chunks.en: And so that the heretics will not say,
chunks.st: And it was also so that the heretics who believe in multiple gods

chunks.en: 'There are many powers in Heaven.'
chunks.st: will not say: There are many authorities in Heaven, and each created a different person.

chunks.he: וּלְהַגִּיד גְּדֻלָּתוֹ שֶׁל הַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא,
chunks.en: And to tell the greatness of Hashem:
chunks.st: And this serves to tell of the greatness of the Holy One, Blessed be He,

chunks.he: שֶׁאָדָם טוֹבֵעַ כַּמָּה מַטְבְּעוֹת בְּחוֹתָם אֶחָד
chunks.en: a person stamps many coins with one stamp,
chunks.st: as when a person stamps several coins with one seal,

chunks.en: and they all look the same.
chunks.st: they are all similar to each other.

chunks.he: וּמֶלֶךְ מַלְכֵי הַמְּלָכִים הַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא
chunks.en: But the King of kings, Hashem,
chunks.st: But the supreme King of kings, the Holy One, Blessed be He,

chunks.he: טָבַע כָּל אָדָם בְּחוֹתָמוֹ שֶׁל אָדָם הָרִאשׁוֹן
chunks.en: stamped every person with the stamp of Adam HaRishon,
chunks.st: stamped all people with the seal of Adam the first man, as all of them are his offspring,

chunks.en: and not one of them looks like another.
chunks.st: and not one of them is similar to another.

chunks.he: לְפִיכָךְ כָּל אֶחָד וְאֶחָד חַיָּב לוֹמַר,
chunks.en: So each and every person must say,
chunks.st: Therefore, since all humanity descends from one person, each and every person is obligated to say:

chunks.en: 'The world was created for me.'
chunks.explain: So I must act in a way that is worthy of it.
chunks.st: The world was created for me,
chunks.stMore: as one person can be the source of all humanity, and recognize the significance of his actions.

chunks.he: וְשֶׁמָּא תֹאמְרוּ מַה לָּנוּ וְלַצָּרָה הַזֹּאת,
chunks.en: And maybe you will say, 'Why do we need this trouble?'
chunks.st: The court says to the witnesses: And perhaps you will say: Why would we want this trouble?
chunks.stMore: Perhaps it would be better not to testify at all.

chunks.en: But it already says,
chunks.st: But be aware, as is it not already stated:

chunks.he: וְהוּא עֵד אוֹ רָאָה אוֹ יָדָע
chunks.en: 'And he is a witness, or he saw, or he knew,
chunks.st: “And he being a witness, whether he has seen or known,

chunks.en: if he does not tell...'
chunks.explain: It is a sin not to testify.
chunks.st: if he does not utter it,
chunks.stMore: then he shall bear his iniquity” (Leviticus 5:1)? It is a transgression not to testify when one can do so.

chunks.en: And maybe you will say, 'Why should we
chunks.st: And perhaps you will say: Why would we want

chunks.en: be blamed for this man's blood?'
chunks.st: to be responsible for the blood of this person?

chunks.en: But it already says,
chunks.st: But be aware, as is it not already stated:

chunks.en: 'When the wicked are lost, there is joyful song.'"
chunks.st: “When the wicked perish, there is song” (Proverbs 11:10)?

mishnayos.summary: In a life-and-death case, the judges ask the witnesses seven main questions about when and where it happened, and other questions about what exactly happened.

chunks.en: They would check the witnesses with seven questions:
chunks.st: The court would examine the witnesses in capital cases with seven interrogations, i.e., interrogatory questions, and they are:

chunks.en: In which seven-year cycle?
chunks.st: In which seven-year
chunks.stMore: period, that is, in which cycle of seven years within a jubilee did the event occur;

chunks.en: In which year?
chunks.st: in which year of the Sabbatical cycle did the event occur;

chunks.en: In which month?
chunks.st: in which month did the event occur;

chunks.en: On which day of the month?
chunks.st: on which day of the month did the event occur;

chunks.en: On which day of the week?
chunks.st: on which day of the week did the event occur;

chunks.en: At what hour?
chunks.st: at which hour did the event occur;

chunks.en: In what place?
chunks.st: and in what place did the event occur.

chunks.en: Rabbi Yosei says, only: On which day?
chunks.st: Rabbi Yosei says: The court would examine the witnesses with only three interrogations: On which day did the event occur,

chunks.en: At what hour?
chunks.st: at which hour,

chunks.en: In what place?
chunks.st: and in what place.

chunks.en: "Do you recognize him?"
chunks.st: They would also ask: Do you recognize him as the man who committed the transgression?

chunks.en: "Did you warn him?"
chunks.st: Did you warn him?
chunks.stMore: They would then ask the witnesses about the particulars of the incident. For example, in the case of

chunks.en: For someone who served idols, they ask:
chunks.st: one who is an accused idol worshipper, they ask the witnesses:

words.note: Avodah zarah: serving idols.

chunks.en: Which idol did he serve,
chunks.st: Whom, i.e., which idol, did he worship,

chunks.en: and how did he serve it?
chunks.st: and in what manner did he worship it, and so on.

mishnayos.summary: A judge who asks the witnesses many extra questions is praised. The mishnah explains the difference between the main questions and the extra ones.

chunks.en: Whoever asks many extra questions,
chunks.st: With regard to all judges who increase the number of examinations,
chunks.stMore: i.e., who add questions about the details of the event,

chunks.en: is praised.
chunks.st: this is praiseworthy,
chunks.stMore: as this may clarify that the witnesses are lying.

chunks.he: מַעֲשֶׂה וּבָדַק בֶּן זַכַּאי בְּעֻקְצֵי תְאֵנִים.
chunks.en: Once ben Zakkai even checked them about the stems of figs.
chunks.st: An incident occurred and ben Zakkai examined the witnesses by questioning them about the color and shape of the stems of figs
chunks.stMore: in order to unearth a contradiction between the witnesses.

words.note: Rabban Yochanan ben Zakkai.

chunks.en: And what is the difference between main questions and extra questions?
chunks.st: The mishna explains: What is the difference between interrogations and examinations?

chunks.en: In the main questions, if one says "I do not know,"
chunks.st: With regard to interrogations, if one of the witnesses says: I do not know the answer,

chunks.en: their testimony does not count.
chunks.st: their testimony is void immediately.

chunks.en: In the extra questions, if one says "I do not know,"
chunks.st: With regard to examinations, if one says: I do not know the answer,

chunks.he: וַאֲפִלּוּ שְׁנַיִם אוֹמְרִים אֵין אָנוּ יוֹדְעִין,
chunks.en: and even if two say "We do not know,"
chunks.st: and even if two say: We do not know the answer,

chunks.en: their testimony still counts.
chunks.st: their testimony still stands.

chunks.en: In both the main and the extra questions,
chunks.st: Both with regard to interrogations and examinations,

chunks.en: when they say things that go against each other,
chunks.st: at a time when the witnesses contradict one another,

chunks.en: their testimony does not count.
chunks.st: their testimony is void.

mishnayos.summary: Small differences between witnesses, like one day or one hour, can be honest mistakes, so the testimony still counts. Bigger differences cancel the testimony.

chunks.en: If one says, "On the second of the month,"
chunks.st: The mishna clarifies: If one witness says the event occurred on the second of the month,

chunks.en: and one says, "On the third of the month,"
chunks.st: and one witness says that the event occurred on the third of the month, this is not regarded as a contradiction and

chunks.en: their testimony counts,
chunks.st: their testimony stands, since it is possible to say

chunks.en: because this one knows that the month was made longer,
chunks.st: that this witness knows of the addition of a day to the previous month,
chunks.stMore: and according to his tally the event occurred on the second of the month,

chunks.he: וְזֶה אֵינוֹ יוֹדֵעַ בְּעִבּוּרוֹ שֶׁל חֹדֶשׁ.
chunks.en: and that one does not know that the month was made longer.
chunks.st: and that witness does not know of the addition of a day to the previous month,
chunks.stMore: and according to his tally the event occurred on the third of the month. Their testimony is not considered incongruent.

chunks.he: אֶחָד אוֹמֵר בִּשְׁלֹשָׁה וְאֶחָד אוֹמֵר בַּחֲמִשָּׁה,
chunks.en: If one says, "On the third," and one says, "On the fifth,"
chunks.st: By contrast, if this witness says the event occurred on the third of the month and one witness says the event occurred on the fifth of the month,

chunks.en: their testimony does not count.
chunks.st: their testimony is void,
chunks.stMore: as this disparity cannot be attributed to a mere error. Therefore, their testimony is not congruent.

chunks.en: If one says, "At the second hour,"
chunks.st: Similarly, if one witness says that the event occurred at two hours,
chunks.stMore: i.e., the second hour of the day from sunrise,

chunks.en: and one says, "At the third hour,"
chunks.st: and one witness says that the event occurred at three hours,

chunks.en: their testimony counts.
chunks.st: their testimony stands,
chunks.stMore: as one could reasonably err this amount in estimating the hour of the day.

chunks.he: אֶחָד אוֹמֵר בְּשָׁלֹשׁ וְאֶחָד אוֹמֵר בְּחָמֵשׁ,
chunks.en: If one says, "At three," and one says, "At five,"
chunks.st: By contrast, if one says that the event occurred at three hours, and one says that the event occurred at five hours,

chunks.en: their testimony does not count.
chunks.st: their testimony is void.

chunks.en: Rabbi Yehudah says, it counts.
chunks.st: Rabbi Yehuda says: Also in this case their testimony stands,
chunks.stMore: as one could reasonably err concerning even this length of time.

chunks.he: אֶחָד אוֹמֵר בְּחָמֵשׁ וְאֶחָד אוֹמֵר בְּשֶׁבַע,
chunks.en: If one says, "At five," and one says, "At seven,"
chunks.st: Rabbi Yehuda adds: But if one says that the event occurred at five hours, and one says that the event occurred at seven hours,

chunks.en: their testimony does not count,
chunks.st: their testimony is void.

chunks.he: שֶׁבְּחָמֵשׁ חַמָּה בַמִּזְרָח וּבְשֶׁבַע חַמָּה בַמַּעֲרָב:
chunks.en: because at five the sun is in the east, and at seven the sun is in the west.
chunks.explain: Nobody would mix those up.
chunks.st: Here the difference is recognizable to all, since at five hours the sun is in the east and at seven the sun is in the west,
chunks.stMore: and one could not err concerning this. Therefore, their testimony is not congruent.

mishnayos.summary: After the witnesses are checked, the judges start by looking for a reason to save the accused. A student with a good reason to save him may join the judges, and even the accused may speak for himself.

chunks.en: Afterward they bring in the second witness
chunks.st: The mishna continues: And afterward, after the court examines the first witness, they bring in the second witness

chunks.en: and check him.
chunks.st: and examine him.

chunks.en: If what they say matches,
chunks.st: If the statements of the witnesses are found to be congruent, the court begins to deliberate the matter.

chunks.en: they start with a reason for "not guilty."
chunks.st: They open the deliberations with an appeal to anyone who can find a reason to acquit the accused.

chunks.en: If one of the witnesses said,
chunks.st: If one of the witnesses said:

chunks.en: "I have a reason to say he is not guilty,"
chunks.st: I can teach a reason to acquit him,

chunks.en: or one of the students said,
chunks.st: or if one of the students sitting before the judges said:

chunks.en: "I have a reason to say he is guilty,"
chunks.st: I can teach a reason to deem him liable,

chunks.en: they quiet him.
chunks.st: the judges silence him,
chunks.stMore: i.e., both the witness and the student. The reason is that these people are not allowed to offer information such as this.

chunks.en: If one of the students said,
chunks.st: But if one of the students said:

chunks.en: "I have a reason to say he is not guilty,"
chunks.st: I can to teach a reason to acquit him,

chunks.en: they bring him up and seat him among them,
chunks.st: they raise him to the seat of the court and seat him among them,

chunks.en: and he would not go down from there
chunks.st: and he would not descend from there

chunks.en: the whole day.
chunks.st: the entire day,
chunks.stMore: but would sit and participate in their deliberations.

chunks.en: If there is real sense in his words,
chunks.st: If the statement of that student has substance,

chunks.en: they listen to him.
chunks.st: the court listens to him.

chunks.en: And even if the accused himself says,
chunks.st: And if even the accused says:

chunks.he: יֶשׁ לִי לְלַמֵּד עַל עַצְמִי זְכוּת,
chunks.en: "I have a reason to say I am not guilty,"
chunks.st: I can teach a reason to acquit me,

chunks.en: they listen to him,
chunks.st: the court listens to him and considers his statement,

chunks.en: as long as there is real sense in his words.
chunks.st: provided that his statement has substance.

mishnayos.summary: If the judges cannot yet find the accused not guilty, they wait until the next day, think it over all night, and vote again. If the vote is very close, more judges are added.

chunks.en: If they found a reason he is not guilty, they let him go.
chunks.st: And if the court found it fit to acquit him during the deliberations, as all or a majority of the judges agreed to acquit him, they excuse him.

chunks.en: And if not,
chunks.st: But if a majority does not find it fit to acquit him,

chunks.en: they put off his case until tomorrow.
chunks.st: they delay his verdict to the following day,

chunks.en: The judges would meet in pairs,
chunks.st: and they then assign pairs
chunks.stMore: of judges to discuss the matter with each other.

chunks.en: and eat only a little,
chunks.st: They would minimize their food intake

chunks.he: וְלֹא הָיוּ שׁוֹתִין יַיִן כָּל הַיּוֹם,
chunks.en: and they would not drink wine the whole day,
chunks.st: and they would not drink wine all day.

chunks.en: and they would discuss it all night.
chunks.st: And they would deliberate all night,

chunks.en: The next day they get up early and come to court.
chunks.st: and the following day they would arise early and come to court
chunks.stMore: and then vote again and tally the votes of the judges.

chunks.en: The one who said "not guilty" says, "I said not guilty,
chunks.st: One who yesterday was of the opinion to acquit the defendant says: I said to acquit,

words.en: the one who says not guilty

chunks.en: and I still say not guilty."
chunks.st: and I acquit in my place, i.e., I stand by my statement to acquit.

chunks.en: And the one who said "guilty" says, "I said guilty,
chunks.st: And one who yesterday was of the opinion to deem him liable says: I said to deem him liable,

words.en: and the one who says guilty

chunks.en: and I still say guilty."
chunks.st: and I deem him liable in my place.

chunks.en: The one who gave a reason for "guilty" may give a reason for "not guilty,"
chunks.st: One who yesterday taught a reason to deem him liable may then teach a reason to acquit,

chunks.en: but the one who gave a reason for "not guilty"
chunks.st: but one who yesterday taught a reason to acquit

chunks.en: may not switch back to "guilty."
chunks.st: may not then teach a reason to deem him liable.

chunks.en: If they made a mistake about what they said,
chunks.st: If they erred in the matter,
chunks.stMore: as one of the judges forgot what he had said the previous day,

chunks.en: the two scribes of the judges remind them.
chunks.st: two judges’ scribes, who recorded the statements of the judges, remind him.

chunks.en: If they found a reason he is not guilty, they let him go.
chunks.st: If the court then found it fit to acquit him unanimously, they excuse him,

chunks.en: And if not,
chunks.st: and if not all of the judges determine to acquit,

chunks.en: they stand up to vote.
chunks.st: they stand to count the vote.

chunks.he: שְׁנֵים עָשָׂר מְזַכִּין וְאַחַד עָשָׂר מְחַיְּבִין, זַכַּאי.
chunks.en: If twelve say "not guilty" and eleven say "guilty," he is not guilty.
chunks.st: If twelve judges vote to acquit him and eleven judges deem him liable, he is acquitted.

chunks.he: שְׁנֵים עָשָׂר מְחַיְּבִין וְאַחַד עָשָׂר מְזַכִּין,
chunks.en: If twelve say "guilty" and eleven say "not guilty,"
chunks.st: The mishna continues: In a case where twelve judges deem him liable and eleven judges acquit;

chunks.en: or even if eleven say "not guilty,"
chunks.st: or even if eleven judges acquit

chunks.en: and eleven say "guilty,"
chunks.st: and eleven deem him liable

chunks.en: and one says "I do not know,"
chunks.st: and one judge says: I do not know;

chunks.en: or even if twenty-two say "not guilty"
chunks.st: or even if twenty-two judges acquit

chunks.en: or say "guilty,"
chunks.st: or deem him liable

chunks.en: and one says "I do not know,"
chunks.st: and one judge says: I do not know,

chunks.en: they must add more judges.
chunks.st: the judge who said he does not know is disregarded, and the judges add
chunks.stMore: additional judges to the court until they reach a definitive ruling.

chunks.en: Up to how many do they add?
chunks.st: And how many judges do they add?

chunks.en: Two at a time, up to seventy-one.
chunks.st: They add pairs of two judges each time they do not reach a ruling until there are seventy-one judges, but no more than that.

chunks.he: שְׁלֹשִׁים וְשִׁשָּׁה מְזַכִּין וּשְׁלֹשִׁים וַחֲמִשָּׁה מְחַיְּבִין, זַכַּאי.
chunks.en: If thirty-six say "not guilty" and thirty-five say "guilty," he is not guilty.
chunks.st: At that point, if thirty-six judges acquit and thirty-five judges deem him liable, he is acquitted.

chunks.he: שְׁלֹשִׁים וְשִׁשָּׁה מְחַיְּבִין וּשְׁלֹשִׁים וַחֲמִשָּׁה מְזַכִּין,
chunks.en: If thirty-six say "guilty" and thirty-five say "not guilty,"
chunks.st: If thirty-six judges deem him liable and thirty-five judges acquit,

chunks.he: דָּנִין אֵלּוּ כְּנֶגֶד אֵלּוּ עַד שֶׁיִּרְאֶה
chunks.en: these and those discuss it, until
chunks.st: they continue to deliberate the matter, these judges against those judges,

chunks.en: one of those who say "guilty" agrees with those who say "not guilty."
chunks.explain: We do not give a death penalty when the majority is only one judge.
chunks.st: until one of those who deems him liable sees the validity of the statements of those who acquit
chunks.stMore: and changes his position, as the court does not condemn a defendant to death by a majority of one judge.

mishnayos.summary: Even on the way to the punishment, the court keeps trying to save the person. A man waits with a flag and another on a horse, ready to stop everything if anyone finds a new reason to say "not guilty."

chunks.en: When the case is finished,
chunks.st: When the trial has ended
chunks.stMore: in a guilty verdict and the condemned man has been sentenced to be stoned,

chunks.en: they take him out for his punishment of stoning.
chunks.st: he is taken out to be stoned.

chunks.he: בֵּית הַסְּקִילָה הָיָה חוּץ לְבֵית דִּין,
chunks.en: The place of stoning was outside the court,
chunks.st: The place of stoning was outside the court and a little beyond it,

chunks.en: as it says,
chunks.st: as it is stated with regard to a blasphemer:

chunks.en: "Take out the one who cursed."
chunks.st: “Take out him who has cursed
chunks.stMore: to outside the camp, and let all that heard him lay their hands upon his head, and let all the congregation stone him” (Leviticus 24:14).

chunks.he: אֶחָד עוֹמֵד עַל פֶּתַח בֵּית דִּין
chunks.en: One man stands at the door of the court
chunks.st: One man stands at the entrance to the court,

chunks.en: with flags in his hand,
chunks.st: with cloths [vehasudarin] in his hand,

chunks.en: and another man rides a horse
chunks.st: and another man sits on a horse

chunks.en: far away from him, but where he can still see him.
chunks.st: at a distance from him but where he can still see him.

chunks.en: If one of the judges says,
chunks.st: If one of the judges says:

chunks.en: "I have a reason to say he is not guilty,"
chunks.st: I can teach a reason to acquit him,

chunks.en: that man waves the flags,
chunks.st: the other, i.e., the man with the cloths, waves the cloths as a signal to the man on the horse,

chunks.en: and the horse runs and stops them.
chunks.st: and the horse races off after the court agents who are leading the condemned man to his execution, and he stops them,
chunks.stMore: and they wait until the court determines whether or not the argument has substance.

chunks.en: And even if he himself says,
chunks.st: And even if he, the condemned man himself, says:

chunks.he: יֶשׁ לִי לְלַמֵּד עַל עַצְמִי זְכוּת,
chunks.en: "I have a reason to say I am not guilty,"
chunks.st: I can teach a reason to acquit myself,

chunks.he: מַחֲזִירִין אוֹתוֹ אֲפִלּוּ אַרְבָּעָה וַחֲמִשָּׁה פְעָמִים,
chunks.en: they bring him back, even four or five times,
chunks.st: he is returned to the courthouse, even four or five times,

chunks.en: as long as there is real sense in his words.
chunks.st: provided that there is substance to his words.
chunks.stMore: If, after the condemned man is returned to the courthouse, the judges

chunks.en: If they found a reason he is not guilty, they let him go.
chunks.st: find a reason to acquit him, they acquit him and release him immediately.

chunks.en: And if not,
chunks.st: But if they do not find a reason to acquit him,

chunks.en: he goes out for his punishment.
chunks.st: he goes out to be stoned.

chunks.en: And a man calls out in front of him:
chunks.st: And a crier goes out before him and publicly proclaims:

chunks.en: "So-and-so, the son of so-and-so,
chunks.st: So-and-so, son of so-and-so,

chunks.he: יוֹצֵא לִסָּקֵל עַל שֶׁעָבַר עֲבֵרָה פְלוֹנִית,
chunks.en: is going out to be punished for doing such-and-such a sin,
chunks.st: is going out to be stoned because he committed such and such a transgression.

chunks.en: and so-and-so and so-and-so are his witnesses.
chunks.st: And so-and-so and so-and-so are his witnesses.

chunks.en: Anyone who knows a reason to say he is not guilty
chunks.st: Anyone who knows of a reason to acquit him

chunks.en: should come and say it."
chunks.st: should come forward and teach it on his behalf.

mishnayos.summary: Before his punishment, the person is told to do teshuvah and confess his sins, so he will have a share in Olam Haba. We learn this from Achan in the days of Yehoshua.

chunks.he: הָיָה רָחוֹק מִבֵּית הַסְּקִילָה כְּעֶשֶׂר אַמּוֹת,
chunks.en: When he was about ten amos from the place,
chunks.st: When the condemned man is at a distance of about ten cubits from the place of stoning,

chunks.en: they say to him, "Confess your sins,"
chunks.st: they say to him: Confess your transgressions,

chunks.en: because that is the way of those who are punished: they confess.
chunks.st: as the way of all who are being executed is to confess.

chunks.he: שֶׁכָּל הַמִּתְוַדֶּה יֶשׁ לוֹ חֵלֶק לָעוֹלָם הַבָּא.
chunks.en: Because anyone who confesses has a share in Olam Haba.
chunks.st: As whoever confesses and regrets his transgressions has a portion in the World-to-Come.

words.note: Olam Haba.

chunks.he: שֶׁכֵּן מָצִינוּ בְעָכָן שֶׁאָמַר לוֹ יְהוֹשֻׁעַ,
chunks.en: That is what we find with Achan, when Yehoshua said to him,
chunks.st: For so we find with regard to Achan, that Joshua said to him:

words.note: He took things from Yericho that Hashem had forbidden.

chunks.he: בְּנִי שִׂים נָא כָבוֹד לַה' אֱלֹהֵי יִשְׂרָאֵל
chunks.en: "My son, please give honor to Hashem, the God of Yisrael,
chunks.st: “My son, please give glory to the Lord, God of Israel,

chunks.en: and confess to Him..."
chunks.st: and make confession to Him” (Joshua 7:19). And the next verse states:

chunks.en: And Achan answered Yehoshua and said,
chunks.st: “And Achan answered Joshua, and said:

chunks.he: אָמְנָה אָנֹכִי חָטָאתִי לַה' אֱלֹהֵי יִשְׂרָאֵל
chunks.en: "It is true, I sinned to Hashem, the God of Yisrael,
chunks.st: Indeed I have sinned against the Lord, God of Israel,

chunks.en: and this and that I did."
chunks.st: and like this and like that have I done.”

chunks.en: And how do we know his confession got him forgiveness?
chunks.st: And from where is it derived that Achan’s confession achieved atonement for him?

chunks.en: As it says,
chunks.st: It is derived from here, as it is stated:

chunks.en: "And Yehoshua said, Why did you bring trouble on us?
chunks.st: “And Joshua said: Why have you brought trouble on us?

chunks.en: Hashem will trouble you on this day."
chunks.st: The Lord shall trouble you this day” (Joshua 7:25).

chunks.en: This day you are troubled,
chunks.st: Joshua said to Achan as follows: On this day of your judgment you are troubled,

chunks.en: but you are not troubled in Olam Haba.
chunks.st: but you will not be troubled in the World-to-Come.

chunks.en: And if he does not know how to confess,
chunks.st: And if the condemned man does not know how to confess, either from ignorance or out of confusion,

chunks.en: they say to him,
chunks.st: they say to him:

chunks.he: אֱמֹר תְּהֵא מִיתָתִי כַפָּרָה עַל כָּל עֲוֹנוֹתָי.
chunks.en: "Say: May my death be a kaparah for all my sins."
chunks.st: Say simply: Let my death be an atonement for all my sins.

chunks.en: Rabbi Yehudah says,
chunks.st: Rabbi Yehuda says:

chunks.en: if he knew that the witnesses lied about him,
chunks.st: If the condemned man knows that he was convicted by the testimony of conspiring witnesses, but in fact he is innocent,

words.note: The witnesses were false.

chunks.he: אוֹמֵר תְּהֵא מִיתָתִי כַּפָּרָה עַל כָּל עֲוֹנוֹתַי
chunks.en: he says, "May my death be a kaparah for all my sins
chunks.st: he says: Let my death be an atonement for all my sins

chunks.en: except for this sin."
chunks.st: except for this sin.

chunks.en: They said to him, "If so,
chunks.st: The Sages who disagreed with Rabbi Yehuda said to him: If so,

chunks.en: everyone would say that
chunks.st: every person who is being executed will say that,

chunks.en: to make themselves look innocent."
chunks.st: to clear himself
chunks.stMore: in the eyes of the public. Therefore, if the condemned man does not make such a statement on his own, the court does not suggest it to him as an alternative.

mishnayos.summary: Close to the place of the punishment, his clothes were taken off. Rabbi Yehudah and the Sages argue about how a man and a woman are covered for modesty.

chunks.he: הָיָה רָחוֹק מִבֵּית הַסְּקִילָה אַרְבַּע אַמּוֹת,
chunks.en: When he was four amos from the place,
they take off his clothes.
A man is covered in front,
and a woman in front and in back.
That is what Rabbi Yehudah says.
But the Sages say,
a man is punished without his clothes,
but a woman is not punished without her clothes.

mishnayos.summary: This mishnah describes how the punishment of stoning was done, and which people were hung up afterward. The body must be taken down and buried the same day, so that Hashem's name is not shamed.

chunks.he: בֵּית הַסְּקִילָה הָיָה גָבוֹהַּ שְׁתֵּי קוֹמוֹת.
chunks.en: The place of stoning was twice as high as a person.

chunks.he: אֶחָד מִן הָעֵדִים דּוֹחֲפוֹ עַל מָתְנָיו.
chunks.en: One of the witnesses pushes him down.
If he turned onto his front,
he turns him onto his back.
If he died from this, that is enough.
And if not,
the second witness takes the stone
and drops it on him.
If he died from this, that is enough.
And if not,
it is finished by all Yisrael,
as it says,

chunks.he: יַד הָעֵדִים תִּהְיֶה בּוֹ בָרִאשֹׁנָה לַהֲמִיתוֹ
chunks.en: "The hand of the witnesses shall be first against him,
and the hand of all the people afterward."
Everyone who is stoned is hung up after he dies.
That is what Rabbi Eliezer says.
But the Sages say,
only the one who cursed Hashem is hung,
and the one who served idols.

chunks.he: הָאִישׁ תּוֹלִין אוֹתוֹ פָּנָיו כְּלַפֵּי הָעָם,
chunks.en: A man is hung facing the people,
and a woman facing the wood,
That is what Rabbi Eliezer says.
But the Sages say,
a man is hung, but a woman is not hung.
Rabbi Eliezer said to them,
"But Shimon ben Shatach

words.note: A great leader in the time of the second Beis HaMikdash.

chunks.en: hang women in Ashkelon!"
They said to him,
"He hung eighty women,
and a court may not judge two people on the same day."
chunks.explain: So that was a special punishment for a very hard time.

chunks.en: How do they hang him?
They put a pole into the ground
with a piece of wood sticking out of it,

chunks.he: וּמַקִּיף שְׁתֵּי יָדָיו זוֹ עַל גַּבֵּי זוֹ
chunks.en: and he puts his two hands one on top of the other
and hangs him.
Rabbi Yosei says,
the pole leans on the wall,
and he hangs him the way butchers hang meat.
And they untie him right away.
And if he stayed there overnight,
they break a mitzvah of the Torah,
as it says,
"His body shall not stay overnight on the wood,
but you shall surely bury him,
because one who is hung is a shame to Hashem."
This means: Why is this one hung?
Because he cursed Hashem.

words.note: This is a polite way to say "cursed."

chunks.en: And so Hashem's name would be shamed.

mishnayos.summary: Hashem feels pain even when a wicked person is punished, and even more for a tzaddik. So we must not leave anyone unburied overnight, except to honor him. Those punished by the court were buried in special places.

chunks.en: Rabbi Meir said,
