chunks.st: Rabbi Meir said:
chunks.stMore: The phrase “for he that is hung is a curse [kilelat] of God” should be understood as follows:

chunks.en: when a person is in pain,
chunks.st: When a man suffers in the wake of his sin,

chunks.en: what does the Shechinah say, so to speak?
chunks.st: what expression does the Divine Presence use?

words.note: Hashem's Presence.

chunks.en: "My head is heavy,
chunks.st: I am distressed [kallani] about My head,

chunks.en: my arm is heavy."
chunks.explain: It means: I too am in pain.
chunks.st: I am distressed about My arm,
chunks.stMore: meaning, I, too, suffer when the wicked are punished.

chunks.en: If Hashem is in pain
chunks.st: From here it is derived: If God suffers such distress

chunks.en: about the blood of wicked people that was spilled,
chunks.st: over the blood of the wicked that is spilled,
chunks.stMore: even though they justly deserved their punishment, it can be inferred

chunks.he: קַל וָחֹמֶר עַל דָּמָם שֶׁל צַדִּיקִים.
chunks.en: how much more so about the blood of tzaddikim!
chunks.st: a fortiori that He suffers distress over the blood of the righteous.

words.note: Even more so.

chunks.en: And not only this,
chunks.st: And the Sages said not only this,
chunks.stMore: that an executed transgressor must be buried on the same day that he is killed,

chunks.en: but anyone who leaves his relative who passed away unburied overnight
chunks.st: but they said that anyone who leaves his deceased relative overnight with-out burying him

chunks.en: breaks a mitzvah of the Torah.
chunks.st: transgresses a prohibition.

chunks.he: הֱלִינוֹ לִכְבוֹדוֹ לְהָבִיא לוֹ אָרוֹן וְתַכְרִיכִים,
chunks.en: If he waited overnight for his honor, to bring him a coffin and shrouds,
chunks.st: But if he left the deceased overnight for the sake of the deceased’s honor, e.g., to bring a coffin or shrouds for his burial,

words.note: Special clothes for burial.

chunks.en: he does not break it.
chunks.st: he does not transgress
chunks.stMore: the prohibition against leaving him unburied overnight.

chunks.he: וְלֹא הָיוּ קוֹבְרִין אוֹתוֹ בְּקִבְרוֹת אֲבוֹתָיו,
chunks.en: They would not bury him in the graves of his fathers,
chunks.st: After the executed transgressor is taken down he is buried, and they would not bury him in his ancestral burial plot.

chunks.en: but two graveyards
chunks.st: Rather, two graveyards

chunks.en: were set up for the court,
chunks.st: were established for the burial of those executed by the court:

chunks.en: one for those killed by the sword and by choking,
chunks.st: One for those who were killed by decapitation or strangled,

chunks.en: and one for those stoned and burned.
chunks.st: and one for those who were stoned or burned.

mishnayos.summary: Later the family gathered the bones and buried them in the family's place. The relatives would greet the judges and witnesses to show they were not angry, because the judgment was true.

chunks.en: After a long time, when only bones were left,
chunks.st: Once the flesh of the deceased had decomposed,

chunks.he: מְלַקְּטִין אֶת הָעֲצָמוֹת וְקוֹבְרִין אוֹתָן בִּמְקוֹמָן.
chunks.en: they gather the bones and bury them in their proper place.
chunks.st: they would gather his bones and bury them in their proper place in his ancestral burial plot.

chunks.en: And the relatives come and greet the judges
chunks.st: And soon after the execution, the relatives of the executed transgressor would come and inquire about the welfare of the judges

chunks.en: and greet the witnesses,
chunks.st: and about the welfare of the witnesses,

chunks.en: as if to say, "We have nothing in our hearts against you,
chunks.st: as if to say: We hold no grudges against you,

chunks.en: because you judged a true judgment."
chunks.st: as you judged a true judgment.

chunks.en: And they would not keep the halachos of mourning,
chunks.st: And the relatives of the executed man would not mourn
chunks.stMore: him with the observance of the usual mourning rites, so that his unmourned death would atone for his transgression;

chunks.en: but they would feel sad,
chunks.st: but they would grieve over his passing,

chunks.en: because sadness is only in the heart.
chunks.st: since grief is felt only in the heart.

mishnayos.summary: The court had four kinds of death penalty. The Tanna Kamma and Rabbi Shimon list them in different orders, from the most severe to the least.

chunks.en: Four kinds of death penalty were given to the court:
chunks.st: Four types of the death penalty were given over to the court,
chunks.stMore: with which those who committed certain transgressions are executed. They are, in descending order of severity:

chunks.en: stoning, burning,
chunks.st: Stoning, burning,

chunks.en: the sword, and choking.
chunks.st: killing by decapitation, and strangulation.

chunks.en: Rabbi Shimon says,
chunks.st: Rabbi Shimon says: They are, in descending order of severity:

chunks.en: burning, stoning,
chunks.st: Burning, stoning,

chunks.en: choking, and the sword.
chunks.st: strangulation, and killing.

chunks.en: What we learned before is how stoning is done.
chunks.st: This execution, described in the previous chapter, is referring to the mitzva of those who are stoned, i.e., to the process of execution by stoning.

mishnayos.summary: This mishnah tells how the punishment of burning was done by the court. Rabbi Yehudah and Rabbi Elazar ben Tzadok add their opinions.

chunks.en: How the punishment of burning is done:

chunks.he: הָיוּ מְשַׁקְּעִין אוֹתוֹ בַזֶּבֶל עַד אַרְכֻּבּוֹתָיו
chunks.en: They would stand him in soft ground up to his knees,
chunks.explain: So he could not move.

chunks.en: and they put a hard cloth inside a soft one
and wrap it around his neck.

chunks.he: זֶה מוֹשֵׁךְ אֶצְלוֹ וְזֶה מוֹשֵׁךְ אֶצְלוֹ
chunks.en: This one pulls it toward himself and that one pulls it toward himself
until he opens his mouth.
And he lights a wick
and puts it into his mouth,
and it goes down inside him
and burns him inside.
Rabbi Yehudah says,
if he died while they were holding him,

chunks.he: לֹא הָיוּ מְקַיְּמִין בּוֹ מִצְוַת שְׂרֵפָה,
chunks.en: they did not do the mitzvah of burning.
Instead, they open his mouth with tongs
against his will,
and he lights the wick
and puts it into his mouth,

chunks.he: וְיוֹרֶדֶת לְתוֹךְ מֵעָיו וְחוֹמֶרֶת אֶת בְּנֵי מֵעָיו.
chunks.en: and it goes down inside him and burns him.
Rabbi Elazar ben Tzadok said,
"Once a daughter of a Kohen did a terrible sin,
and they put bundles of branches around her and burned her."
They said to him,
"That was because the court
of that time did not know the halachah well."

mishnayos.summary: This mishnah tells how the punishments of the sword and of choking were done by the court.

chunks.en: How the punishment of the sword is done:
They would cut off his head with a sword,
the way the kingdom does.
Rabbi Yehudah says,
that is a disgrace.

chunks.he: אֶלָּא מַנִּיחִין אֶת רֹאשׁוֹ עַל הַסַּדָּן
chunks.en: Instead, they put his head on a block
and cut with an axe.
They said to him,
"No death is more of a disgrace than that."
How the punishment of choking is done:

chunks.he: הָיוּ מְשַׁקְּעִין אוֹתוֹ בַזֶּבֶל עַד אַרְכֻּבּוֹתָיו
chunks.en: They would stand him in soft ground up to his knees,
and they put a hard cloth inside a soft one
and wrap it around his neck.

chunks.he: זֶה מוֹשֵׁךְ אֶצְלוֹ וְזֶה מוֹשֵׁךְ אֶצְלוֹ,
chunks.en: This one pulls toward himself and that one pulls toward himself,
until his soul goes out.

mishnayos.summary: This mishnah lists the people who get the punishment of stoning, like one who serves idols, breaks Shabbos, or curses his father or mother, and those who did certain forbidden relationships.

chunks.en: These are the ones who are stoned:
one who sins with his mother,

words.note: Who does a forbidden relationship.

chunks.en: or with his father's wife,
or with his daughter-in-law,
or with a man,
or with an animal,
and a woman who sins with an animal,
and one who curses Hashem, and one who serves idols,

words.en: and the one who curses Hashem

chunks.en: and one who gives his child to the Molech,

words.note: An idol that children were given to.

chunks.en: and a ba'al ov and a yidoni,

words.note: A kind of witchcraft that claims to talk with the dead.
Another kind of witchcraft.

chunks.en: and one who breaks Shabbos,
and one who curses his father or his mother,
and one who sins with a girl who is engaged,

words.note: She had kiddushin but the wedding had not happened yet.

chunks.en: and one who tempts others to serve idols, and one who leads a whole city to serve idols,

words.note: He tempts a person to serve idols.

words.en: and the one who leads astray
words.note: He leads a whole city to serve idols.

chunks.en: and a sorcerer, and a ben sorer u'moreh.

words.note: A boy who steals and eats and drinks wildly, taught in the next perek.

chunks.en: One who sins with his mother
is chayav for her because she is his mother,
and because she is his father's wife.
Rabbi Yehudah says,

chunks.he: אֵינוֹ חַיָּב אֶלָּא מִשּׁוּם הָאֵם בִּלְבָד.
chunks.en: he is chayav only because she is his mother.
One who sins with his father's wife
is chayav because she is his father's wife
and because she is a married woman,
whether while his father is alive
or after his father passed away,

chunks.he: בֵּין מִן הָאֵרוּסִין בֵּין מִן הַנִּשּׂוּאִין.
chunks.en: whether she was only engaged or already married to him.
One who sins with his daughter-in-law
is chayav because she is his daughter-in-law
and because she is a married woman,
whether while his son is alive
or after his son passed away,

chunks.he: בֵּין מִן הָאֵרוּסִין בֵּין מִן הַנִּשּׂוּאִין.
chunks.en: whether she was only engaged or already married to him.
One who sins with a man or with an animal,
and a woman who sins with an animal, are stoned.
If the person sinned,
what did the animal do wrong?
But because a person came
to a terrible sin through it,
that is why the Torah says it shall be stoned.
Another reason:

chunks.he: שֶׁלֹּא תְהֵא בְּהֵמָה עוֹבֶרֶת בַּשּׁוּק וְיֹאמְרוּ
chunks.en: so that an animal will not walk through the market, and people will say,

chunks.he: זוֹ הִיא שֶׁנִּסְקַל פְּלוֹנִי עַל יָדָהּ:
chunks.en: "This is the one because of which so-and-so was stoned."
chunks.explain: That would shame the person who was punished.

mishnayos.summary: One who curses Hashem is only punished if he used Hashem's real name. The judges are very careful never to say the curse more than needed, and they tear their clothes when they hear it.

chunks.he: הַמְגַדֵּף אֵינוֹ חַיָּב עַד שֶׁיְּפָרֵשׁ הַשֵּׁם.
chunks.en: One who curses Hashem is not chayav unless he says Hashem's name clearly.
chunks.st: One who blasphemes, i.e., one who curses God, is not liable unless he utters the name of God and curses it.

chunks.en: Rabbi Yehoshua ben Korchah said,
chunks.st: Rabbi Yehoshua ben Korḥa said:

chunks.en: Every day of the case, they question the witnesses
chunks.st: On every day of a blasphemer’s trial, when the judges judge the witnesses, i.e., interrogate the witnesses,

chunks.en: using another name: "Let Yosei hit Yosei."
chunks.explain: Instead of saying Hashem's name in the curse.
chunks.st: they ask the witnesses to use an appellation for the name of God, so that they do not utter a curse of God’s name. Specifically, the witnesses would say: Let Yosei smite Yosei,
chunks.stMore: as the name Yosei has four letters in Hebrew, as does the Tetragrammaton.

chunks.en: When the case is finished,
chunks.st: When the judgment is over,
chunks.stMore: and the court votes to deem the defendant guilty,

chunks.en: they do not punish him because of the nickname.
chunks.st: they do not sentence him to death based on the testimony of the witnesses in which they used an appellation
chunks.stMore: for the name of God, without having ever heard the exact wording of the curse.

chunks.en: Instead, they send everyone outside
chunks.st: Rather, they remove all the people
chunks.stMore: who are not required to be there from the court, so that the curse is not heard publicly,

chunks.en: and they ask the oldest of the witnesses,
chunks.st: and the judges interrogate the eldest of the witnesses,

chunks.he: וְאוֹמְרִים לוֹ אֱמֹר מַה שֶּׁשָּׁמַעְתָּ בְּפֵרוּשׁ,
chunks.en: and they say to him, "Say exactly what you heard."
chunks.st: and say to him: Say what you heard explicitly.

chunks.en: And he says it.
chunks.st: And he says exactly what he heard.

chunks.en: And the judges stand on their feet
chunks.st: And the judges stand on their feet

chunks.en: and tear their clothes, and never sew them back.
chunks.explain: To show how terrible it is to curse Hashem.
chunks.st: and make a tear in their garments, as an act of mourning for the desecration of the honor of God. And they do not ever fully stitch it back together again.

chunks.en: And the second witness says, "I heard the same as him."
chunks.st: And the second witness says: I too heard as he
chunks.stMore: did, but he does not repeat the curse explicitly.

chunks.en: And the third witness says, "I heard the same as him."
chunks.st: And the third witness, in the event that there is one, says: I too heard as he
chunks.stMore: did. In this manner, the repetition of the invective sentence is limited to what is absolutely necessary.

mishnayos.summary: One who serves an idol in one of the ways Hashem is served, or in the idol's own special way, gets the punishment of stoning. Other kinds of honor to an idol are also forbidden, but without the death penalty.

chunks.en: One who serves idols:
whether one who serves it,
or one who slaughters an animal for it,
or one who burns incense for it,
or one who pours wine for it,
or one who bows to it,
or one who accepts it as his god,
or one who says to it, "You are my god."

chunks.he: אֲבָל הַמְגַפֵּף וְהַמְנַשֵּׁק וְהַמְכַבֵּד וְהַמְּרַבֵּץ וְהַמַּרְחִיץ,
chunks.en: But one who hugs it, kisses it, cleans it, sprinkles water before it, washes it,
rubs it with oil, dresses it, or puts shoes on it,

words.en: the one who rubs with oil
and the one who puts shoes on

chunks.en: breaks a mitzvah of the Torah.
One who makes a promise in its name or swears in its name
breaks a mitzvah of the Torah.
One who does the disgusting act for Ba'al Peor is stoned,

words.note: An idol served in a very disgusting way.

chunks.en: because that is how it is served.
One who throws a stone at Markulis is stoned,

words.note: An idol that people served by throwing stones at it.

chunks.en: because that is how it is served.

mishnayos.summary: One who gives his child to the Molech is only chayav if he does both parts of that idol's service. The mishnah also explains two kinds of witchcraft.

chunks.en: One who gives his child to the Molech
chunks.st: One who gives of his offspring to Molekh, for which one is executed by stoning,

chunks.en: is not chayav until he hands him over to the Molech
chunks.st: is not liable unless he hands over his child to the priests of Molekh

chunks.en: and passes him through the fire.
chunks.st: and passes the child through the fire.

chunks.en: If he handed him over to the Molech but did not pass him through the fire,
chunks.st: If he handed over the child to the priests of Molekh but did not pass him through the fire,

chunks.en: or passed him through the fire but did not hand him over to the Molech,
chunks.st: or if he passed him through the fire but did not hand him over to the priests of Molekh,

chunks.en: he is not chayav,
chunks.st: he is not liable,

chunks.en: until he hands him over to the Molech and passes him through the fire.
chunks.st: unless he hands the child over to the priests of Molekh and passes him through the fire.
chunks.stMore: The list of those liable to be executed by stoning includes those who practice various types of sorcery. The mishna describes them:

chunks.he: בַּעַל אוֹב זֶה פִתּוֹם הַמְדַבֵּר מִשֶּׁחְיוֹ,
chunks.en: A ba'al ov is a pisom who seems to speak from his armpit,
chunks.st: A necromancer is a pitom from whose armpit the voice of the dead appears to speak.

words.note: A kind of sorcerer.

chunks.en: and a yidoni is one who speaks with his mouth.
chunks.st: And a sorcerer is one from whose mouth the dead appears to speak.

chunks.en: These are stoned,
chunks.st: These, the necromancer and the sorcerer, are executed by stoning,

chunks.en: and one who asks them questions breaks a mitzvah of the Torah.
chunks.st: and one who inquires about the future through them is in violation of a prohibition.

mishnayos.summary: One who breaks Shabbos is stoned only for a melachah that brings kareis. One who curses his father or mother is stoned only if he used Hashem's name.

chunks.en: One who breaks Shabbos
chunks.st: Also liable to be executed by stoning is one who desecrates Shabbat

chunks.en: by doing something that, done on purpose, brings kareis,
chunks.st: by performing a matter that for its intentional performance one is liable to receive karet

words.note: A punishment from Heaven of being cut off.

chunks.en: and done by mistake, needs a korban chatas.
chunks.st: and for its unwitting performance one is obligated to bring a sin-offering.

words.note: A korban brought for a sin done by mistake.

chunks.en: One who curses his father or his mother
chunks.st: One who curses his father or his mother

chunks.en: is not chayav unless he curses them with Hashem's name.
chunks.st: is not liable to be executed by stoning unless he curses them with the name of God.

chunks.en: If he cursed them using another name of Hashem,
chunks.st: If he cursed them with an appellation of the name of God,

chunks.en: Rabbi Meir says he is chayav, and the Sages say he is patur.
chunks.st: Rabbi Meir deems him liable, and the Rabbis deem him exempt.

mishnayos.summary: This mishnah explains exactly when the punishment of stoning is given for a forbidden relationship with an engaged girl.

chunks.en: One who sins with a girl who is engaged

words.note: Who does a forbidden relationship.

chunks.en: is not chayav unless she is a young girl,
never married before, and engaged,
and she is still in her father's house.
If two men sinned with her,
the first is stoned, and the second is choked.

mishnayos.summary: A meisis is someone who tries to talk another person into serving idols. This is the only case where the court may hide witnesses to catch him. A maddiach leads a whole city to serve idols.

chunks.en: The meisis is a regular person
chunks.st: With regard to the case of an inciter, listed among those liable to be executed by stoning, this is an ordinary person, not a prophet.

chunks.en: who tempts another regular person.
chunks.st: And it is referring to one who incites an ordinary person and not a multitude of people.

chunks.he: אָמַר לוֹ יֵשׁ יִרְאָה בְמָקוֹם פְּלוֹנִי,
chunks.en: He says to him, "There is an idol in such-and-such a place.
chunks.st: What does the inciter do? He says: There is an idol in such and such a place, which

chunks.en: This is how it eats, this is how it drinks,
chunks.st: eats like this, drinks like this,

chunks.en: this is how it does good, this is how it does harm."
chunks.st: does good for its worshippers like this, and harms those who do not worship it like this.
chunks.stMore: The mishna states a principle with regard to the halakha of an inciter: With regard to

chunks.en: For everyone in the Torah who can get a death penalty,
chunks.st: all of those mentioned in the Torah who are liable to receive the death
chunks.stMore: penalty, if there are no witnesses to their transgressions,

chunks.en: we do not hide witnesses to catch them, except for this one.
chunks.st: the court does not hide witnesses in order to ensnare and punish them, except for this case of an inciter.

chunks.en: If he said it to two people, they are his witnesses,
chunks.st: The mishna elaborates: If the inciter said his words of incitement to two men, they are his witnesses, and
chunks.stMore: he does not need to be warned before the transgression;

chunks.he: מְבִיאִין אוֹתוֹ לְבֵית דִּין וְסוֹקְלִין אוֹתוֹ.
chunks.en: and they bring him to court and stone him.
chunks.st: they bring him to court and stone him.

chunks.en: If he said it to only one,
chunks.st: If he said his words of incitement to one
chunks.stMore: man alone, that man’s testimony would not be sufficient to have the inciter executed.

chunks.he: הוּא אוֹמֵר יֶשׁ לִי חֲבֵרִים רוֹצִים בְּכָךְ.
chunks.en: he says to him, "I have friends who want this too."
chunks.st: Therefore he says to the inciter: I have friends who are interested in this;
chunks.stMore: tell them too. This way there will be more witnesses.

chunks.en: If he is sly
chunks.st: The mishna continues: If the inciter is cunning,

chunks.en: and will not speak in front of them,
chunks.st: and he knows that he cannot speak in front of two men,

chunks.en: they hide witnesses for him behind the fence,
chunks.st: the court hides witnesses for him behind the fence so that he will not see them,

chunks.en: and he says to him,
chunks.st: and the man whom the inciter had previously tried to incite says to him:

chunks.en: "Say what you told me in private."
chunks.st: Say what you said to me when we were in seclusion.

chunks.en: And the meisis says it to him,
chunks.st: And the other person, the inciter, says to him again that he should worship the idol.

chunks.en: and he answers him,
chunks.st: And he says to the inciter:

chunks.en: "How can we leave our God in Heaven
chunks.st: How can we forsake our God in Heaven

chunks.en: and go and serve wood and stones?"
chunks.st: and go and worship wood and stones?

chunks.he: אִם חוֹזֵר בּוֹ, הֲרֵי זֶה מוּטָב.
chunks.en: If he takes it back, that is good.
chunks.st: If the inciter retracts his suggestion, that is good.

chunks.en: But if he says, "This is our duty,
chunks.st: But if he says: This idol worship is our duty;

chunks.en: and this is good for us,"
chunks.st: this is what suits us,

chunks.en: those standing behind the fence
chunks.st: then those standing behind the fence

chunks.he: מְבִיאִין אוֹתוֹ לְבֵית דִּין וְסוֹקְלִין אוֹתוֹ.
chunks.en: bring him to court and stone him.
chunks.st: bring him to court and have him stoned.

chunks.en: A meisis is one who says, "I will serve,"
chunks.st: The halakha of an inciter includes one who says: I shall worship idols, or one of the following statements:

chunks.en: "I will go and serve," "Let us go and serve,"
chunks.st: I shall go and worship idols, or: let us go and worship idols,

chunks.en: "I will sacrifice," "I will go and sacrifice," "Let us go and sacrifice,"
chunks.st: or: I shall sacrifice an idolatrous offering, or: I shall go and sacrifice an idolatrous offering, or: Let us go and sacrifice an idolatrous offering,

chunks.en: "I will burn incense," "I will go and burn incense," "Let us go and burn incense,"
chunks.st: or: I shall burn incense as an idolatrous offering, or: I shall go and burn incense, or: Let us go and burn incense,

chunks.en: "I will pour wine," "I will go and pour," "Let us go and pour,"
chunks.st: or: I shall pour an idolatrous libation, or: I shall go and pour a libation, or: Let us go and pour a libation,

chunks.en: "I will bow," "I will go and bow," "Let us go and bow."
chunks.st: or: I shall bow to an idol, or: I shall go and bow, or: Let us go and bow.

chunks.en: The maddiach is one who says to many people,
chunks.st: With regard to the case of the subverter listed among those liable to be executed by stoning, this is one who says to a multitude of people:

chunks.en: "Let us go and serve idols."
chunks.st: Let us go and worship idols.

mishnayos.summary: A sorcerer who really does magic is stoned, but one who only fools people's eyes is not. Rabbi Akiva gives an example with two people gathering cucumbers.

chunks.en: A sorcerer who really does an act is chayav,
chunks.st: The warlock is also liable to be executed by stoning. One who performs a real act of sorcery is liable,

chunks.en: but not one who only fools the eyes.
chunks.st: but not one who deceives the eyes,
chunks.stMore: making it appear as though he is performing sorcery, as that is not considered sorcery.

words.note: Does tricks that only look like magic.

chunks.he: רַבִּי עֲקִיבָא אוֹמֵר מִשּׁוּם רַבִּי יְהוֹשֻׁעַ,
chunks.en: Rabbi Akiva says in the name of Rabbi Yehoshua,
chunks.st: Rabbi Akiva says in the name of Rabbi Yehoshua:

chunks.en: two people gather cucumbers by magic.
chunks.st: For example, two people can each gather cucumbers by sorcery.

chunks.he: אֶחָד לוֹקֵט פָּטוּר וְאֶחָד לוֹקֵט חַיָּב,
chunks.en: One who gathers is patur, and one who gathers is chayav.
chunks.st: One of them gathers cucumbers and he is exempt, and the other one gathers cucumbers and he is liable.

chunks.en: The one who really does an act is chayav,
chunks.st: How so? The one who performs a real act of sorcery is liable,

chunks.en: the one who only fools the eyes is patur.
chunks.st: and the one who deceives the eyes is exempt.

mishnayos.summary: The Torah tells of a ben sorer u'moreh, a wayward and rebellious son. This mishnah teaches that this halachah is only for a boy, and only for a short time right after he becomes bar mitzvah.

chunks.en: A wayward and rebellious son:
From when does he become a ben sorer u'moreh?

chunks.he: מִשֶּׁיָּבִיא שְׁתֵּי שְׂעָרוֹת וְעַד שֶׁיַּקִּיף זָקָן,
chunks.en: From when he shows signs of growing up, until his beard grows all around,

words.note: Signs that a boy has grown up.

chunks.en: the lower one and not the upper one,
chunks.explain: Another sign of growing older, not the beard on his face.

chunks.en: but the Sages spoke in clean, polite words,
as it says,
"If a man has a son":
a son and not a daughter,
a son and not a grown man.
A young child is patur,
because he is not yet old enough for mitzvos.

mishnayos.summary: A ben sorer u'moreh is only punished if he steals and eats a lot of meat and drinks a lot of wine in a wild way. If his meal was for a mitzvah, or was forbidden food, he is not.

chunks.en: From when is he chayav?
chunks.st: From when is a stubborn and rebellious son liable?

chunks.en: From when he eats a tarteimar of meat
chunks.st: From when he eats a tarteimar of meat

words.note: A certain amount.

chunks.en: and drinks half a log of Italian wine.
chunks.st: and drinks a half-log of Italian wine.

words.note: A measure of liquid.

chunks.en: Rabbi Yosei says,
chunks.st: Rabbi Yosei says: From when he eats

chunks.en: a maneh of meat and a log of wine.
chunks.st: a maneh of meat and drinks a log of wine.
chunks.stMore: The mishna now lists a series of conditions concerning his eating and drinking. If

words.note: A bigger amount.

chunks.en: If he ate at a mitzvah meal,
chunks.st: he ate these items with a group assembled for the performance of a mitzva,

chunks.en: or ate at the meal for making the month longer,
chunks.st: or he ate them at a meal celebrating the intercalation of a month,

chunks.en: or ate maaser sheni in Yerushalayim,
chunks.explain: Since these are mitzvah meals, he is not a ben sorer.
chunks.st: or he ate the items when they had second tithe status, in Jerusalem,
chunks.stMore: he does not become a stubborn and rebellious son because each of these circumstances involves some aspect of a mitzva.

chunks.en: or ate neveilos and treifos,
chunks.st: If he ate the meat of unslaughtered animal carcasses or animals that had wounds that would have caused them to die within twelve months [tereifot]

words.note: Animals that died without shechitah.
Animals with a deadly injury.

chunks.en: or bugs and creeping things,
chunks.st: or repugnant creatures or creeping animals,

chunks.en: or ate tevel,
chunks.st: or he ate untithed produce
chunks.stMore: from which tithes and terumot were not separated,

words.note: Food that terumah and maaser were not taken from yet.

chunks.en: or maaser rishon whose terumah was not taken off,
chunks.st: or first tithe from which its teruma was not separated,

words.note: First tithe, given to the Levi'im.

chunks.en: or maaser sheni and hekdesh that were not redeemed,
chunks.explain: Since these are sins, he is not a ben sorer.
chunks.st: or second tithe outside Jerusalem or consecrated food that was not redeemed,
chunks.stMore: each of which involves a transgression, he does not become a stubborn and rebellious son.

chunks.en: If he ate something that is a mitzvah
chunks.st: The mishna summarizes: If he ate an item that involves performing a mitzva

chunks.en: or something that is a sin,
chunks.st: or an item that involves committing a transgression,

chunks.he: אָכַל כָּל מַאֲכָל וְלֹא אָכַל בָּשָׂר,
chunks.en: or he ate any food but did not eat meat,
chunks.st: or if he ate any food in the world but did not eat meat,

chunks.he: שָׁתָה כָל מַשְׁקֶה וְלֹא שָׁתָה יַיִן,
chunks.en: or drank any drink but did not drink wine,
chunks.st: or if he drank any beverage but did not drink wine,

chunks.en: he does not become a ben sorer u'moreh,
chunks.st: he does not become a stubborn and rebellious son,

chunks.en: until he eats meat and drinks wine,
chunks.st: unless he actually eats meat and actually drinks wine,

chunks.en: as it says,
chunks.st: as it is stated:
chunks.stMore: “This son of ours is stubborn and rebellious; he does not listen to our voice; he…

chunks.en: "a glutton and a drunkard."
chunks.st: is a glutton [zolel] and a drunkard [vesovei]”
chunks.stMore: (Deuteronomy 21:20). One is not called a glutton and a drunkard unless he eats meat and drinks wine.

chunks.he: וְאַף עַל פִּי שֶׁאֵין רְאָיָה לַדָּבָר,
chunks.en: And even though there is no proof for this,
chunks.st: And although there is no explicit proof to the matter
chunks.stMore: that the reference in the Torah is to meat and wine,

chunks.en: there is a hint to it,
chunks.st: there is an allusion to the matter in another verse,

chunks.en: as it says,
chunks.st: as it is stated:

chunks.en: "Do not be among those who drink too much wine,
chunks.st: “Be not among wine drinkers [besovei],

chunks.en: among those who eat too much meat."
chunks.st: among gluttonous eaters [bezolelei] of meat” (Proverbs 23:20).

mishnayos.summary: He only becomes a ben sorer u'moreh if he steals from his father and eats it somewhere else.

chunks.he: גָּנַב מִשֶּׁל אָבִיו וְאָכַל בִּרְשׁוּת אָבִיו,
chunks.en: If he stole from his father and ate in his father's place,
chunks.st: If he stole that which belonged to his father and ate on his father’s property,

chunks.en: or from others and ate in others' place,
chunks.st: or he stole that which belonged to others and ate on the property of others,

chunks.en: or from others and ate in his father's place,
chunks.st: or he stole that which belonged to others and ate on his father’s property,

chunks.en: he does not become a ben sorer u'moreh,
chunks.st: he does not become a stubborn and rebellious son,

chunks.en: until he steals from his father
chunks.st: unless he steals that which belonged to his father

chunks.en: and eats in someone else's place.
chunks.st: and eats on the property of others.

chunks.he: רַבִּי יוֹסֵי בַר רַבִּי יְהוּדָה אוֹמֵר,
chunks.en: Rabbi Yosei the son of Rabbi Yehudah says,
chunks.st: Rabbi Yosei, son of Rabbi Yehuda, says:

chunks.he: עַד שֶׁיִּגְנֹב מִשֶּׁל אָבִיו וּמִשֶּׁל אִמּוֹ:
chunks.en: until he steals from his father and from his mother.
chunks.st: He does not become a stubborn and rebellious son unless he steals that which belonged to his father and that which belonged to his mother.

mishnayos.summary: Both parents must want their son judged, and both must be able to do everything the pasuk says. The son is first warned and given lashes, and only if he does it again is he judged.

chunks.he: הָיָה אָבִיו רוֹצֶה וְאִמּוֹ אֵינָהּ רוֹצָה,
chunks.en: If his father wants it and his mother does not,
or his father does not want it and his mother does,
he does not become a ben sorer u'moreh,
until both of them want it.
Rabbi Yehudah says,

chunks.he: אִם לֹא הָיְתָה אִמּוֹ רְאוּיָה לְאָבִיו,
chunks.en: if his mother was not a fitting match for his father,
he does not become a ben sorer u'moreh.

chunks.he: הָיָה אֶחָד מֵהֶם גִּדֵּם אוֹ חִגֵּר
chunks.en: If one of them had no hands, or was lame,

chunks.he: אוֹ אִלֵּם אוֹ סוּמָא אוֹ חֵרֵשׁ,
chunks.en: or could not speak, or was blind, or deaf,
he does not become a ben sorer u'moreh,
as it says,
"And his father and his mother shall take hold of him"
and not those without hands.
"And they shall take him out"
and not those who are lame.
"And they shall say," and not those who cannot speak.
"This son of ours,"
and not those who are blind.
"He does not listen to our voice,"
and not those who are deaf.

chunks.he: מַתְרִין בּוֹ בִּפְנֵי שְׁלֹשָׁה וּמַלְקִין אוֹתוֹ.
chunks.en: They warn him in front of three judges and give him lashes.
If he went back and did it again,
he is judged by twenty-three.
And he is not stoned
unless the first three judges are there,
as it says,
"This son of ours":
this is the one who got lashes in front of you.
If he ran away before his case was finished,

chunks.he: וְאַחַר כָּךְ הִקִּיף זָקָן הַתַּחְתּוֹן, פָּטוּר.
chunks.en: and then he grew older, he is patur.
But if he ran away after his case was finished,

chunks.he: וְאַחַר כָּךְ הִקִּיף זָקָן הַתַּחְתּוֹן, חַיָּב:
chunks.en: and then he grew older, he is chayav.

mishnayos.summary: The ben sorer u'moreh is judged because of what he will surely become. Then the mishnah teaches how some things are good when the wicked have them, but bad when tzaddikim have them, and the opposite.

chunks.he: בֵּן סוֹרֵר וּמוֹרֶה נִדּוֹן עַל שֵׁם סוֹפוֹ,
chunks.en: A ben sorer u'moreh is judged because of how he will end up.
chunks.explain: He will surely become a robber and hurt people.
chunks.st: A stubborn and rebellious son is sentenced to death not because of the severity of the transgression that he already committed but on account of his ultimate end,
chunks.stMore: because a boy of his nature will grow up to lead an immoral life, and it is better that

chunks.en: Better he should die innocent, and not die guilty,
chunks.st: he should die while he is still innocent, before causing excessive harm, and not die after he becomes guilty.

chunks.en: because the death of wicked people
chunks.st: This is because the death of the wicked

chunks.en: is good for them and good for the world,
chunks.explain: Now they cannot sin any more.
chunks.st: is beneficial to them, because they can no longer sin, and it is also beneficial to the world, which is now rid of those who do it harm.

chunks.en: but for tzaddikim it is bad for them and bad for the world.
chunks.st: Conversely, the death of the righteous is detrimental to them, as they can no longer engage in the performance of mitzvot, and it is also detrimental to the world, as the righteous are now absent from it.

chunks.en: Wine and sleep for wicked people
chunks.st: By way of association, the mishna continues: The wine and sleep of the wicked

chunks.en: are good for them and good for the world,
chunks.explain: While they drink or sleep, they do not hurt anyone.
chunks.st: are beneficial to them and beneficial to the world,
chunks.stMore: as when they are sleeping or under the influence of wine, they do not cause harm to others.

chunks.en: but for tzaddikim they are bad for them and bad for the world.
chunks.st: And, conversely, the wine and sleep of the righteous are detrimental to them and detrimental to the world,
chunks.stMore: as wine and sleep prevent them from engaging in their good deeds.

chunks.en: Being spread apart, for wicked people,
chunks.st: The dispersal of the wicked,
chunks.stMore: so that they are not found in close proximity to each other,

chunks.en: is good for them and good for the world,
chunks.st: is beneficial to them, as they are less likely to provoke each other to sin, and it is beneficial to the world.

chunks.en: but for tzaddikim it is bad for them and bad for the world.
chunks.st: The dispersal of the righteous is detrimental to them and detrimental to the world.

chunks.en: Gathering together, for wicked people,
chunks.st: The assembly of the wicked in one place

chunks.en: is bad for them and bad for the world,
chunks.st: is detrimental to them and detrimental to the world,

chunks.en: but for tzaddikim it is good for them and good for the world.
chunks.st: while the assembly of the righteous is beneficial to them and beneficial to the world.

chunks.en: Quiet and calm, for wicked people,
chunks.st: The tranquility of the wicked

chunks.en: is bad for them and bad for the world,
chunks.st: is detrimental to them and detrimental to the world,

chunks.en: but for tzaddikim it is good for them and good for the world.
chunks.st: while the tranquility of the righteous is beneficial to them and beneficial to the world.

mishnayos.summary: A thief who breaks into a house is judged by what he might do in the end. If he broke a barrel on the way in, whether he must pay depends on whether the owner was allowed to stop him.

chunks.he: הַבָּא בַמַּחְתֶּרֶת נִדּוֹן עַל שֵׁם סוֹפוֹ.
chunks.en: One who breaks in through a tunnel is judged because of how he might end up.
chunks.explain: He might hurt the owner, so the owner may stop him even by killing him.
chunks.st: A burglar who is found breaking into a house may be killed by the owner of the house with impunity (see Exodus 22:1). He too is sentenced on account of his ultimate end,
chunks.stMore: as it is presumed that if the owner of the house would resist the burglar, the burglar would kill the owner of the house.

chunks.he: הָיָה בָא בַמַּחְתֶּרֶת וְשָׁבַר אֶת הֶחָבִית,
chunks.en: If he was breaking in through a tunnel and broke a barrel,
chunks.st: If the burglar was breaking into a house, and in the course of doing so he broke a barrel,

chunks.en: if the owner would be punished for killing him, he must pay.
chunks.st: if there is blood-guiltiness for killing him, i.e., if the homeowner would be liable for killing him, the burglar is liable
chunks.stMore: to pay for the value of the barrel. An example of this is if a father broke into his son’s house, in which case it is presumed that even if the son resists his father, his father would never kill him, and therefore the son may not kill his father, and if he does so he is liable.

chunks.en: If the owner would not be punished for killing him, he is patur.
chunks.st: If there is no blood-guiltiness for killing him, i.e., if the homeowner would be exempt from punishment for killing him, the burglar is exempt from paying for the barrel.

mishnayos.summary: We may stop some people even by taking their lives, to save someone from being killed or from a terrible sin. But we do not do this for other sins, even very serious ones.

chunks.en: These are the ones we save even by taking their lives:
one who chases his friend to kill him,
or chases a man or an engaged girl to do a forbidden sin.
But one who chases an animal for a sin,
and one who is about to break Shabbos,
and one who is about to serve idols,
we do not save them by taking their lives.

mishnayos.summary: This mishnah lists who gets the punishment of burning (certain forbidden relationships) and who gets the sword (a murderer and the people of an ir hanidachas). It also teaches when someone counts as a murderer.

chunks.en: These are the ones who are burned:
one who sins with a woman and her daughter,

words.note: Who does a forbidden relationship.

chunks.en: and a Kohen's daughter who did a forbidden sin.
Under "a woman and her daughter" are included:
his daughter, his daughter's daughter, his son's daughter,

chunks.he: וּבַת אִשְׁתּוֹ, וּבַת בִּתָּהּ, וּבַת בְּנָהּ,
chunks.en: his wife's daughter, her daughter's daughter, her son's daughter,
his mother-in-law, his mother-in-law's mother, and his father-in-law's mother.
And these are the ones killed by the sword:
the murderer, and the people of an ir hanidachas.

words.note: A city where everyone served idols.

chunks.he: רוֹצֵחַ שֶׁהִכָּה אֶת רֵעֵהוּ בְאֶבֶן אוֹ בְבַרְזֶל,
chunks.en: A murderer who hit his friend with a stone or with iron,
or held him down in the water
or in the fire,
and he could not get out of there,
and he died, is chayav.

chunks.he: דְּחָפוֹ לְתוֹךְ הַמַּיִם אוֹ לְתוֹךְ הָאוּר
chunks.en: If he pushed him into the water or into the fire,
and he could have gotten out of there,
and he died, he is patur.
If he sent a dog after him,
or sent a snake after him, he is patur.
If he made the snake bite him,
Rabbi Yehudah says he is chayav,
and the Sages say he is patur.
One who hits his friend,
whether with a stone or with a fist,
and they thought he would die,
and he got better than he was,
and after that he got worse and died, he is chayav.
Rabbi Nechemyah says,
he is patur, because there is a reason to think so.
chunks.explain: Something else may have made him die.

mishnayos.summary: A person is only punished as a murderer if he meant to kill this kind of person, and his blow was strong enough to kill where it landed. The mishnah gives many cases where his plan and what happened do not match.

chunks.en: If he meant to kill an animal
chunks.st: If one intended to kill an animal,

chunks.en: and killed a person,
chunks.st: and he killed a person standing adjacent to it,

chunks.en: or meant to kill a non-Jew and killed a Jew,
chunks.st: or if he intended to kill a gentile, for whose murder he is not liable to be executed in court, and he killed a Jew,

chunks.en: or a baby who could not live and killed one who could live, he is patur.
chunks.st: or if he intended to kill non-viable newborns, for whose murder one is not liable, and he killed a viable person, the assailant is exempt
chunks.stMore: from execution, since his intent was to kill one for whose murder he is not liable.

chunks.en: If he meant to hit him on his waist,
chunks.st: If one intended to strike another on his loins,

chunks.he: וְלֹא הָיָה בָהּ כְּדֵי לְהָמִית עַל מָתְנָיו
chunks.en: and it was not strong enough to kill on his waist,
chunks.st: and the blow was not powerful enough to kill him if it were to land on his loins,

chunks.en: but it landed on his heart,
chunks.st: but instead the blow landed on his chest over the victim’s heart,
